mishnayos.summary: When a man dies with no children, his brother usually does yibum or chalitzah with the widow. This mishnah lists fifteen close relatives of the brother who are free from this, and their co-wives are free too.

chunks.en: Fifteen women free their co-wives

words.note: A co-wife (tzarah) is another wife married to the same husband.

chunks.en: and the co-wives of their co-wives
from chalitzah and from yibum

words.note: A ceremony that frees a widow from yibum.
When a man dies with no children, his brother marries the widow.

chunks.en: forever, all the way down the line.
And these are the women:
his daughter, and his daughter's daughter,
and his son's daughter,
his wife's daughter,
and his wife's son's daughter,
and his wife's daughter's daughter,
his mother-in-law, and his mother-in-law's mother,
and his father-in-law's mother,
his sister from his mother,
and his mother's sister,
and his wife's sister,
and the wife of his brother from his mother,
and the wife of a brother who was not yet born when he lived,
chunks.explain: The second brother was born only after the first one died.

chunks.en: and his daughter-in-law.
These free their co-wives
and the co-wives of their co-wives
from chalitzah and from yibum
forever.
But if any of them died,
chunks.explain: She died before her husband did.

chunks.en: or did mi'un,

words.note: Mi'un: a young girl married off by her mother or brothers may say no to the marriage and end it.

chunks.en: or were divorced,
or turned out to be an aylonis,

words.note: A woman who cannot have children; her marriage was a mistake.

chunks.en: then their co-wives are allowed.
And you cannot say
about his mother-in-law, her mother, or his father-in-law's mother
that they turned out to be an aylonis,
chunks.explain: She has children, so she cannot be an aylonis.

chunks.en: or that they did mi'un.
chunks.explain: Mi'un is only for young girls, who could not be a mother.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah shows how a forbidden relative frees her co-wife, and even the co-wife's co-wife. But if the relative died or was divorced first, her co-wife is not freed.

chunks.en: How do they free their co-wives?
chunks.st: The mishna explains: How do these women exempt their rival wives?

chunks.en: If his daughter, or any one of
chunks.st: If, for example, his daughter or any one of

chunks.en: these forbidden relatives, was married to his brother,
chunks.st: those women with whom relations are forbidden was married to his brother

words.note: Women a man may not marry because they are close family.

chunks.en: and he had another wife,
chunks.st: and this brother had another wife,

chunks.en: and he died, just as his daughter is free,
chunks.st: and the brother died, then just as his daughter is exempt from levirate marriage,

chunks.en: so her co-wife is free.
chunks.st: so too her rival wife is exempt. If

chunks.he: הָלְכָה צָרַת בִּתּוֹ וְנִשֵּׂאת לְאָחִיו הַשֵּׁנִי,
chunks.en: If his daughter's co-wife went and married his second brother,
chunks.st: his daughter’s rival wife subsequently went and married his second brother, to whom she is permitted,

chunks.en: and he had another wife,
chunks.st: and he had another wife,

chunks.en: and he died, just as his daughter's co-wife is free,
chunks.st: and he died childless as well, which means that his wife comes before the first yavam, the daughter’s father, for levirate marriage, then just as his daughter’s rival wife is exempt,

chunks.en: so her co-wife's co-wife is free,
chunks.st: so too the rival wife of her rival wife is exempt. The mishna adds:

chunks.en: even if there are a hundred of them.
chunks.st: Even if they are one hundred brothers, the same logic applies.
chunks.stMore: If a woman is exempt from levirate marriage because she is the rival wife of a forbidden relative or the rival wife of a rival wife of this kind, and she herself has an additional rival wife, this rival wife is also exempt and in turn exempts her own rival wives from levirate marriage.

chunks.en: How is it that if they died, their co-wives are allowed?
chunks.st: How so? What are the cases in which if they died their rival wives are permitted?

chunks.en: If his daughter, or any one of
chunks.st: If, for example, one’s daughter or any one of

chunks.en: these forbidden relatives, was married to his brother,
chunks.st: those women with whom relations are forbidden was married to his brother, and this brother

chunks.en: and he had another wife,
chunks.st: had another wife,

chunks.en: and his daughter died or was divorced,
chunks.st: and then his daughter died or was divorced

chunks.en: and after that his brother died,
chunks.st: and afterward his brother died,

chunks.en: her co-wife is allowed.
chunks.st: her rival wife is permitted to him. §

chunks.en: And any girl who could do mi'un but did not,
chunks.explain: Her marriage was only from the Rabbis, not fully from the Torah.
chunks.st: The mishna states another principle: And if any of these forbidden relatives was a minor who could refuse her husband, then even if she did not refuse,

chunks.en: her co-wife does chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: her rival wife performs ḥalitza and does not enter into levirate marriage.
chunks.stMore: The rival wife may not enter into levirate marriage, as she is the rival wife of a forbidden relative. However, she is not entirely exempt from levirate marriage and must be released by ḥalitza because the marriage of the forbidden relative was not a fully valid marriage, and therefore, by Torah law, the other woman is not considered a rival wife of a forbidden relative.

mishnayos.summary: Six relatives are forbidden even more strictly, because they can never marry any of the brothers. So yibum does not apply at all, and their co-wives are allowed.

chunks.en: Six forbidden relatives are stricter than these,
chunks.st: Six women with whom relations are forbidden who were not enumerated in the first mishna are forbidden by prohibitions that are more severe than those listed in that mishna

chunks.en: because they are married to others,
chunks.explain: They are never married to a brother, so yibum never applies.
chunks.st: because they may be married only to others and may never be married to any of the brothers, due to the closeness of their relationship.
chunks.stMore: However, this stringency entails a corresponding leniency: Since the halakha of levirate marriage is entirely inapplicable in these cases,

chunks.en: so their co-wives are allowed.
chunks.st: their rival wives are permitted.
chunks.stMore: The rival wife of a forbidden relative is forbidden herself only if the mitzva of levirate marriage is applicable, but where it is not in effect she is permitted. The six women with whom relations are forbidden are as follows:

chunks.en: His mother, and his father's wife,
chunks.st: His mother, and his father’s wife,

chunks.en: and his father's sister,
chunks.st: and his father’s sister,

chunks.en: his sister from his father,
chunks.st: and his paternal half sister,

chunks.en: and the wife of his father's brother,
chunks.st: and the wife of his father’s brother,

chunks.en: and the wife of his brother from his father.
chunks.st: and the wife of his paternal half brother.
chunks.stMore: Each of these women with whom relations are forbidden is forbidden equally to all of the brothers, and the mitzva of levirate marriage is inapplicable. Therefore, her rival wife is permitted.

mishnayos.summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue whether these co-wives may marry the brothers. Even so, the two groups still married into each other's families and trusted each other's purity.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai allow the co-wives to the brothers,
chunks.explain: Beis Shammai say the co-wife of a forbidden relative may do yibum.

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel forbid them.

chunks.he: חָלְצוּ, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי פּוֹסְלִין מִן הַכְּהֻנָּה,
chunks.en: If they did chalitzah, Beis Shammai make them unfit to marry a Kohen,
chunks.explain: A woman who did chalitzah may not marry a Kohen.

words.note: Being married to a Kohen.

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say they are fit.
If they did yibum, Beis Shammai say they are fit,
and Beis Hillel make them unfit.
Even though these
forbid and these allow,
these make unfit and these say fit,
Beis Shammai did not stop
marrying women from Beis Hillel,
and Beis Hillel did not stop marrying women from Beis Shammai.
And in all the questions of tahor and tamei,

words.note: Things that are tahor, pure.
Things that are tamei, impure.

chunks.en: where these said tahor and these said tamei,
they did not stop handling pure things
with each other.
chunks.explain: They trusted each other's dishes and food.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah explains "the wife of a brother who was not alive in his lifetime": a brother born after the first brother died does not do yibum with that widow, and her co-wife is freed too.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְעוֹלָמוֹ.
chunks.en: What is "the wife of his brother who was not alive in his lifetime"?
Two brothers,
and one of them died,
and a new brother was born to them,
and after that the second brother did yibum
with his brother's wife,
and then he died.
The first wife goes out because she is the wife of
chunks.explain: Goes out means she is free, with no yibum or chalitzah.

chunks.en: his brother who was not alive in his lifetime,
and the second goes out because she is her co-wife.
If he only made a maamar with her and then died,

words.note: The first step of yibum: the brother says words of kiddushin to her.

chunks.en: the second wife does chalitzah, but not yibum.

mishnayos.summary: Here the new brother was born after the yibum already happened. The Rabbis still free both wives, but Rabbi Shimon says the new brother may do yibum or chalitzah with whichever wife he wants.

chunks.en: Two brothers, and one of them died,
chunks.st: If there were two brothers, and one died,

chunks.en: and the second did yibum with his brother's wife,
chunks.st: and the second entered into levirate marriage with his brother’s wife while he was already married to another woman,

chunks.en: and after that a brother was born to them,
chunks.st: and subsequently a third brother was born to them,

chunks.en: and then he died. The first goes out because she is the wife of
chunks.st: and the second brother then died, whereby both of his wives happened before the third brother for levirate marriage, then the first woman, who was the wife of the first brother, is exempt due to the fact that she is

chunks.en: his brother who was not alive in his lifetime,
chunks.st: the wife of a brother with whom the third brother did not coexist,

chunks.en: and the second because she is her co-wife.
chunks.st: and the second woman, who was the first wife of the second brother, is exempt due to her rival wife.

chunks.en: If he only made a maamar with her,
chunks.st: If the second brother had performed only levirate betrothal with her

chunks.en: and then he died, the second does chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: and then died before fully marrying her, the second woman performs ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage, as the levirate betrothal is not considered a sufficiently valid marriage so as to render her the rival wife of a relation forbidden to the third brother.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says with regard to the first clause of the mishna: The third brother either

chunks.en: he does yibum with whichever one he wants,
chunks.st: enters into levirate marriage with whichever one he wishes,

chunks.en: or does chalitzah with whichever one he wants.
chunks.st: or he performs ḥalitza with whichever one he wishes.
chunks.stMore: Since he was born after his second brother had already entered into levirate marriage with the first brother’s widow, she is considered the wife of a brother with whom he did coexist, not the wife of a brother with whom he did not coexist. Therefore, he may enter into levirate marriage with her.

mishnayos.summary: A rule about a yevamah: if she is a forbidden relative, she is completely free. If she is forbidden only by a smaller prohibition, she does chalitzah but not yibum.

chunks.en: They said a rule about a yevamah:
chunks.st: The Sages stated a principle about a yevama:

words.note: A widow waiting for yibum or chalitzah.

chunks.en: any woman who is a forbidden relative
chunks.st: Whoever is forbidden by a prohibition of forbidden relations to her yavam

chunks.en: does not do chalitzah and does not do yibum.
chunks.st: neither performs ḥalitza nor enters into levirate marriage and is completely exempt.

chunks.en: If her prohibition is "an issur mitzvah"
chunks.st: If she is forbidden by a prohibition resulting from a mitzva

chunks.en: or "an issur kedushah,"
chunks.st: or by a prohibition stemming from sanctity, as will be explained later, then since in these cases the obligation of levirate marriage is not fundamentally nullified

chunks.en: she does chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: she performs ḥalitza in order to become free of the levirate bond, and due to her prohibition she does not enter into levirate marriage.
chunks.stMore: The Sages stated another principle: If two sisters who had been married to two brothers who subsequently died happened before the third brother for levirate marriage, and one of those sisters is a close relation to this third brother and is therefore forbidden to him, she is exempt from levirate marriage.

chunks.en: Her sister, who is also her yevamah,
chunks.explain: Two sisters fall to the same brother, and one is his own close relative.
chunks.st: But the other, her sister who is her yevama, i.e., her sister-in-law,

chunks.en: does chalitzah or yibum.
chunks.st: performs ḥalitza or enters into levirate marriage.
chunks.stMore: In this case, they are not ruled to be two sisters who happened before him simultaneously for levirate marriage, since one of them is prohibited to him as a forbidden relation, and therefore she never actually happened before him at all.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah explains the two smaller prohibitions from the last mishnah: relatives forbidden by the Rabbis, and marriages forbidden because of holiness, like a widow to a Kohen Gadol.

chunks.en: An "issur mitzvah" means
the second-level relatives forbidden by the Rabbis.

words.note: The early Sages.

chunks.en: An "issur kedushah" means
a widow to a Kohen Gadol,

words.note: The Kohen Gadol, the High Priest.

chunks.en: a divorced woman or one who did chalitzah to a regular Kohen,

words.note: A woman who did chalitzah.

chunks.en: a mamzeres or a Nesinah to a Jew,

words.note: A girl born from a forbidden relationship.
From the Givonim, who joined the Jews in Yehoshua's time.

chunks.en: and a Jewish girl to a Nasin or a mamzer.

mishnayos.summary: Any brother, no matter how, counts as a brother for yibum, and any son frees his father's wife from yibum. But not a child born from a non-Jewish mother or a maidservant.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ אָח מִכָּל מָקוֹם,
chunks.en: Anyone who has a brother of any kind
chunks.st: In the case of anyone who has a brother of any kind, that brother

chunks.en: binds his brother's wife to yibum,
chunks.st: creates a levirate bond causing his yevama to be required to perform levirate marriage if the first brother dies childless.

chunks.en: and he is his brother for everything,
chunks.st: And he is his brother in all respects,

chunks.en: except for one who has a brother
chunks.st: except for one who has a brother born

chunks.en: from a maidservant or from a non-Jewish woman.
chunks.explain: Such a child is not counted as his father's family.
chunks.st: from a Canaanite maidservant or from a gentile woman, as these do not have the legal status of brothers.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ בֵּן מִכָּל מָקוֹם,
chunks.en: Anyone who has a child of any kind
chunks.st: Similarly, in the case of anyone who has a child of any kind, that child

chunks.en: frees his father's wife from yibum,
chunks.st: exempts his father’s wife from levirate marriage, since his father did not die childless.

chunks.en: and he is punished if he hits him or curses him,
chunks.st: And that child is liable to receive capital punishment if he strikes his father or curses him.

chunks.en: and he is his son for everything,
chunks.st: And he is his child in all respects,

chunks.en: except for one who has a child
chunks.st: except for whoever has a child born

chunks.en: from a maidservant or from a non-Jewish woman.
chunks.st: from a Canaanite maidservant or from a gentile woman, as these do not have the halakhic status of children.

mishnayos.summary: A man made kiddushin with one of two sisters but does not know which one. He must give each a get, and if he dies, his brothers must be careful with yibum and chalitzah.

chunks.en: Someone who made kiddushin with one of two sisters
chunks.st: In the case of one who betrothed one of two sisters

words.note: The first step of Jewish marriage.

chunks.en: and does not know which of them he married,
chunks.st: and does not know which of them he betrothed, so that both are forbidden to him, he

chunks.en: gives a get to this one and a get to that one.
chunks.st: gives a bill of divorce to this one and a bill of divorce to that one due to the uncertainty. If the man who had betrothed one of these women

words.note: A document of divorce.

chunks.en: If he died and he had one brother,
chunks.st: died before he could give a bill of divorce, and he had one brother, that brother

chunks.en: that brother does chalitzah with both of them.
chunks.explain: He may not do yibum, because one of them may be his yevamah's sister.
chunks.st: performs ḥalitza with both of them, but he may not take either in levirate marriage.
chunks.stMore: This is because he does not know which woman is his yevama and which is forbidden to him as the sister of a woman with whom he has a levirate bond. If the man who betrothed one of these women

chunks.en: If he had two brothers,
chunks.st: had two brothers,

chunks.en: one does chalitzah and one may do yibum.
chunks.st: one of them performs ḥalitza with one of the sisters, but he may not enter into levirate marriage with her due to the possibility that she is the sister of a woman with whom he has a levirate bond. And one takes the other in levirate marriage if he so desires.

chunks.en: If they went ahead and married them first,
chunks.st: If the two brothers married the two sisters before consulting the court, the court does not

chunks.en: we do not take the wives away from them.
chunks.st: remove them from their marriage and they are permitted to remain married.
chunks.stMore: The couple who performed levirate marriage second was even permitted to do so, since there was no longer any doubt about the levirate bond.

mishnayos.summary: Two men each married one of two sisters, but neither knows which one. The mishnah teaches what their brothers do with yibum and chalitzah, depending on how many brothers each one has.

chunks.en: Two men who made kiddushin with two sisters,
chunks.st: Furthermore, in the case of two unrelated men who betrothed two sisters:

chunks.en: this one does not know which one he married,
chunks.st: If this one does not know which sister he betrothed

chunks.en: and that one does not know which one he married,
chunks.st: and that one does not know which sister he betrothed,

chunks.en: this one gives two gittin,
chunks.st: this one gives two bills of divorce, one to each of the women,

words.note: Documents of divorce.

chunks.en: and that one gives two gittin.
chunks.st: and that one gives two bills of divorce.

chunks.en: If they died, and this one had a brother
chunks.st: If the two men died before they divorced, and this one had a brother and

chunks.en: and that one had a brother,
chunks.st: that one had a brother,

chunks.en: this brother does chalitzah with both,
chunks.st: then this brother performs ḥalitza with both of them,

chunks.en: and that brother does chalitzah with both.
chunks.st: and that brother performs ḥalitza with both of them.

chunks.en: If this one had one brother and that one had two,
chunks.st: If this one had one brother and that one had two brothers,

chunks.en: the one brother does chalitzah with both,
chunks.st: the single brother performs ḥalitza with both of them,

chunks.en: and of the two, one does chalitzah and one may do yibum.
chunks.st: and of the two brothers, one performs ḥalitza and one performs levirate marriage if he so desires.

chunks.en: If they went ahead and married first,
chunks.st: If they married the sisters before consulting the court, the court

chunks.en: we do not take the wives away from them.
chunks.st: does not remove them from the marriage and they are not told to divorce them.

chunks.en: If this one had two brothers and that one had two,
chunks.st: If this one had two brothers and that one had two brothers,

chunks.en: this one's brother does chalitzah with one sister,
chunks.st: the brother of this one performs ḥalitza with one sister,

chunks.en: and that one's brother does chalitzah with one sister.
chunks.st: and the brother of that one performs ḥalitza with one sister.

chunks.en: Then this one's other brother may do yibum
chunks.st: The brother of this one who performed ḥalitza

chunks.en: with the one who did chalitzah from that one,
chunks.st: may take the woman who performed ḥalitza [ḥalutza] of that other’s brother in levirate marriage,

chunks.en: and that one's other brother may do yibum
chunks.st: and the brother of that second one who performed ḥalitza

chunks.en: with the one who did chalitzah from this one.
chunks.st: may take the ḥalutza of that other’s brother in levirate marriage.

chunks.en: If two went ahead and both did chalitzah,
chunks.st: If the two brothers performed ḥalitza with both wives before consulting the court,

chunks.en: the other two may not both do yibum,
chunks.st: the two brothers of the second man may not take sisters in levirate marriage lest one marry the sister of a woman who with whom he had a levirate bond.

chunks.en: but one does chalitzah and one may do yibum.
chunks.st: Rather, one performs ḥalitza and one performs levirate marriage if he so desires.

chunks.en: If they went ahead and married first,
chunks.st: If they married their wives before consulting the court, the court

chunks.en: we do not take the wives away from them.
chunks.st: does not remove them from the marriage.

mishnayos.summary: The oldest brother should be the one to do yibum. The mishnah also teaches that a man people suspect of being with a certain woman should not marry her later.

chunks.en: The mitzvah of yibum is on the oldest brother.
But if the younger one went first,
she is his. Someone suspected about a maidservant who was later freed,

words.note: People suspect he had a forbidden relationship with her.

chunks.en: or about a non-Jewish woman who later became a Jew,
should not marry her.
But if he married her, we do not take her away from him.
Someone suspected about a married woman,
and because of it she was taken away from her husband,
even if he married her, he must send her away.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who helps a woman become free to remarry, by bringing her get or by saying her husband died, should not marry her himself, so no one thinks he lied to get her.

chunks.en: Someone who brings a get from overseas
chunks.st: An agent who brought a bill of divorce from a country overseas

chunks.en: and says, "It was written in front of me and signed in front of me,"
chunks.st: and said: It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence, as required in order to establish the bill of divorce as valid,

chunks.en: may not marry that wife.
chunks.st: may not marry the wife, i.e., the divorcée.
chunks.stMore: Since the validity of the bill of divorce is based upon his testimony, marrying the divorcée creates the impression that he had an ulterior motive for his testimony. Similarly, a witness who testified that a certain man

chunks.en: If he says, "He died," or "I killed him,"
chunks.st: died, or testified: I killed him, or:

chunks.en: or "We killed him," he may not marry his wife.
chunks.st: We killed him, may not marry that man’s wife.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: If he testified:

chunks.en: If he said "I killed him," his wife may not remarry.
chunks.explain: Nobody is believed when he says he did something very wrong.
chunks.st: I killed him, his wife may not be married at all based on that evidence, as his testimony is unreliable, but if he said:

chunks.en: If he said "We killed him," his wife may remarry.
chunks.st: We killed him, his wife may be married to anyone other than those witnesses.

mishnayos.summary: A Sage or judge who made a woman forbidden, or helped free her, should not always marry her. The mishnah tells when it is allowed.

chunks.en: A Sage who forbade a woman
chunks.st: A Sage who refused to release a woman from a vow that rendered the wife forbidden to her husband by that

chunks.en: to her husband because of a neder,
chunks.st: vow, resulting in her being divorced from her husband,

words.note: A promise to Hashem.

chunks.en: may not marry her.
chunks.st: may not marry her, so as to avoid suspicion that he rendered her forbidden to her husband in order to marry her himself. However, a judge before whom a woman

chunks.en: If she did mi'un or chalitzah in front of him,
chunks.st: performed refusal when she was a minor, declaring that she did not desire the husband chosen for her by her family, or before whom she performed ḥalitza,

chunks.en: he may marry her, because he was part of a beis din.
chunks.st: may marry her because he was only one member of the court, thereby alleviating suspicion.

words.note: A Jewish court.

chunks.en: And all of them who had wives
chunks.st: And for all of these who were involved in permitting the wife to remarry, i.e., the judge, the agent who brought a bill of divorce, and the one who testified for a woman that her husband died, if they had wives at the time of the ruling or the testimony

chunks.en: and the wives died, are allowed to marry these women.
chunks.st: and their wives died thereafter, then those women they had set free are permitted to be married to them. There is no concern that while their wives were still alive these individuals set their eyes upon another woman.

chunks.he: וְכֻלָּן שֶׁנִּשְּׂאוּ לַאֲחֵרִים וְנִתְגָּרְשׁוּ אוֹ שֶׁנִּתְאַלְמְנוּ,
chunks.en: And all these women who married others and were divorced or widowed
chunks.st: And with regard to all of these women who were prohibited from marrying a certain man due to some suspicion, if they were subsequently married to others and then were divorced or widowed from the second husband,

chunks.en: are allowed to marry them.
chunks.st: they are permitted to be married to them, i.e., to the judge, messenger, or witness who permitted her to remarry.

chunks.en: And all of them are allowed to their sons or brothers.
chunks.st: And all of these women who were prohibited from marrying due to some suspicion are permitted to the sons or to the brothers of those who set them free.

mishnayos.summary: Two brothers married to two sisters died. The remaining brothers may not do yibum with either sister, because each is the sister of a woman tied to them, so they do chalitzah.

chunks.en: Four brothers,
chunks.st: In the case of four brothers,

chunks.en: two of them were married to two sisters,
chunks.st: two of whom were married to two sisters,

chunks.en: and the ones married to the sisters died.
chunks.st: and the ones married to the sisters died,

chunks.en: These sisters do chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.explain: Each sister is tied to the brothers, so her sister is forbidden like a wife's sister.
chunks.st: then those sisters must perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage.
chunks.stMore: Since both sisters require levirate marriage with each of the surviving brothers, a levirate bond exists between each sister and the brothers. Each of them is considered the sister of a woman with whom each brother has a levirate bond and is therefore forbidden to him by rabbinic law.

chunks.en: And if they went ahead and married them,
chunks.st: And if they married the sisters before consulting the court,

chunks.en: they must send them away. Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: they should divorce them, for the Sages decreed that in this situation they may not remain married. Rabbi Eliezer says that there is a dispute in this matter:

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say they may stay married,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say: He may maintain her as his wife,

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say they must send them away.
chunks.st: while Beit Hillel say: They must divorce them.

mishnayos.summary: If one sister is a forbidden relative to one brother, that brother may do yibum with the other sister. But a smaller prohibition does not help, and she does only chalitzah.

chunks.en: If one of them was forbidden
chunks.st: If one of the sisters was forbidden

chunks.en: to one brother as a forbidden relative,
chunks.st: to one of the brothers due to a prohibition against forbidden relations because she was a relative of his wife or a relative on his mother’s side, then

chunks.en: he may not marry her, but he may marry her sister.
chunks.st: he is forbidden to marry her but permitted to marry her sister.
chunks.stMore: Because she is his close relative, she is exempt from levirate marriage with him, and therefore she is not bound to him with a levirate bond. Consequently, her sister is not considered the sister of a woman with whom he has a levirate bond, and he is permitted to enter into levirate marriage with her.

chunks.en: But the second brother is forbidden to both of them. If an issur
chunks.st: But the second brother, who is not a close relative of either sister, is forbidden to marry both of them. Indeed, for him each woman remains the sister of a woman with whom he has a levirate bond. If a prohibition resulting from

chunks.en: mitzvah or issur kedushah is the problem,
chunks.st: a mitzva or a prohibition stemming from sanctity will be transgressed when one of the women marries one of the brothers, then her sister must

chunks.en: she does chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage, as she is considered the sister of a woman with whom he has a levirate bond.
chunks.stMore: In this case, the sister who is forbidden to the brother due to a mitzva or due to sanctity is bound to the brother for the purpose of ḥalitza.

mishnayos.summary: If each sister is a forbidden relative to a different brother, each brother may do yibum or chalitzah with the sister who is not his relative.

chunks.en: If one of them was forbidden
to this brother as a forbidden relative,

chunks.he: וְהַשְּׁנִיָּה אֲסוּרָה עַל זֶה אִסּוּר עֶרְוָה,
chunks.en: and the second was forbidden to that brother as a forbidden relative,
the one forbidden to this one is allowed to that one,
and the one forbidden to that one is allowed to this one.
This is what they meant when they said,
"If her sister is also her yevamah,
she either does chalitzah or yibum."

mishnayos.summary: If two brothers were married to two close relatives, like sisters or a mother and daughter, and both died, the third brother does chalitzah but not yibum. Rabbi Shimon frees them completely.

chunks.en: Three brothers,
chunks.st: In the case of three brothers,

chunks.en: two of them were married to two sisters,
chunks.st: two of whom were married to close relatives, e.g., two sisters;

chunks.en: or a woman and her daughter,
chunks.st: or a woman and her daughter;

chunks.en: or a woman and her daughter's daughter,
chunks.st: or a woman and her daughter’s daughter;

chunks.en: or a woman and her son's daughter.
chunks.st: or a woman and her son’s daughter, if the two brothers who were married to two close relatives died and their wives happened before a third brother for levirate marriage,

chunks.en: These do chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: then these two women must perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage, as each of them is a relative of a woman with whom he has a levirate bond.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Shimon frees them.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Shimon exempts them even from the obligation to perform ḥalitza.

chunks.en: If one of them was forbidden
chunks.st: If one of them was forbidden

chunks.en: to him as a forbidden relative,
chunks.st: to him, the third brother, due to a prohibition against forbidden relatives, then

chunks.en: he may not marry her, but he may marry her sister.
chunks.st: he is prohibited from marrying her but is permitted to marry her sister.
chunks.stMore: Because the woman who is forbidden to him is not considered to be a woman who requires him for levirate marriage, there is only one woman who happens before him for levirate marriage.

chunks.en: If it is an issur mitzvah or an issur kedushah,
chunks.st: However, if one of the women was forbidden due to a prohibition resulting from a mitzva or a prohibition stemming from sanctity, then

chunks.en: they do chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: they must perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage. This is because these prohibitions do not completely cancel the levirate bond.

mishnayos.summary: The single brother made a maamar with one sister, and then the other sister also fell to him. Beis Shammai let him keep the first; Beis Hillel say he loses both, so "woe to him" for both.

chunks.en: Three brothers,
two of them were married to two sisters,
and one was single.
One of the sisters' husbands died,
and the single brother made a maamar with her.
After that, his second brother died.
Beis Shammai say,
"His wife stays with him,
and the other one goes out because she is his wife's sister."
But Beis Hillel say,
"He sends away his wife with a get and chalitzah,
and his brother's wife with chalitzah."
This is what they said:
"Woe to him for his wife, and woe
to him for his brother's wife."

mishnayos.summary: A brother did yibum with his sister-in-law and then died. The last brother is married to her sister, so she is freed, and the other wife is freed as her co-wife. After only a maamar, the other wife does chalitzah.

chunks.en: Three brothers,
two of them were married to two sisters,
and one was married to an unrelated woman.
One of the sisters' husbands died,
and the one married to the unrelated woman married his wife,

chunks.he: וָמֵת, הָרִאשׁוֹנָה יוֹצְאָה מִשּׁוּם אֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה,
chunks.en: and then he died. The first goes out because she is his wife's sister,
and the second goes out because she is her co-wife.
If he only made a maamar with her
and died, the unrelated woman does chalitzah, but not yibum.
Three brothers,
two of them were married to two sisters,
and one was married to an unrelated woman.
The one married to the unrelated woman died,

chunks.he: וְכָנַס אֶחָד מִבַּעֲלֵי אֲחָיוֹת אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ,
chunks.en: and one of the sisters' husbands married his wife,

chunks.he: וָמֵת, הָרִאשׁוֹנָה יוֹצְאָה מִשּׁוּם אֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה,
chunks.en: and then he died. The first goes out because she is his wife's sister,
and the second because she is her co-wife.
If he only made a maamar with her
and died, the unrelated woman does chalitzah, but not yibum.

mishnayos.summary: A woman who was forbidden to a brother even for a short time stays forbidden to him forever. But a relative who was divorced before the husband died does not free her co-wife.

chunks.en: Three brothers,
two of them were married to two sisters,
and one was married to an unrelated woman.
One of the sisters' husbands died,
and the one married to the unrelated woman married his wife.
Then the second brother's wife died,
and after that the one married to the unrelated woman died.
She is forbidden to him forever,
because she was forbidden to him for one moment.
chunks.explain: When she first fell to him, she was his wife's sister.

chunks.en: Three brothers,
two of them were married to two sisters,
and one was married to an unrelated woman.

chunks.he: גֵּרֵשׁ אֶחָד מִבַּעֲלֵי אֲחָיוֹת אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ,
chunks.en: One of the sisters' husbands divorced his wife,
and the one married to the unrelated woman died,
and the one who had divorced married her,
and then he died. This is what they said,
chunks.explain: Now the last brother may do yibum with the unrelated woman.

chunks.en: "And all of them who died or were divorced,
their co-wives are allowed."

mishnayos.summary: If it is not sure whether a forbidden relative was really married or really divorced, her co-wife must do chalitzah but not yibum. The mishnah gives examples of such doubtful kiddushin and doubtful gittin.

chunks.en: And any of them who had kiddushin
chunks.st: And if any of these fifteen women who are prohibited as forbidden relatives

chunks.en: or a get that was in doubt,
chunks.st: had undergone a betrothal or divorce whose status is uncertain with the deceased brother,

chunks.en: their co-wives
chunks.st: then those women who were their rival wives must

chunks.en: do chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage since they are possibly the rival wives of forbidden relatives.

chunks.en: How can kiddushin be in doubt?
chunks.st: The mishna elaborates: How could there be a situation of uncertainty with regard to betrothal? If in the public domain

chunks.en: If he threw her the kiddushin,
chunks.explain: He threw her a ring or coin across a street.
chunks.st: he threw her an item for the purpose of betrothal and there were eight cubits between them, and the item

chunks.he: סָפֵק קָרוֹב לוֹ סָפֵק קָרוֹב לָהּ,
chunks.en: and it may have landed nearer to him or nearer to her,
chunks.st: was possibly closer to him and did not enter into her domain, and possibly closer to her, i.e., within four cubits of her, whereby she could acquire the object,

chunks.en: that is a doubtful kiddushin.
chunks.st: this is a case of uncertainty with regard to betrothal.

chunks.en: A doubtful get:
chunks.st: Uncertainty with regard to divorce occurs when, for instance,

chunks.he: כָּתַב בִּכְתַב יָדוֹ וְאֵין עָלָיו עֵדִים,
chunks.en: he wrote it in his own handwriting, but no witnesses signed it,
chunks.st: he wrote a bill of divorce in his handwriting but there are no signatures of witnesses on the document,

chunks.he: יֵשׁ עָלָיו עֵדִים וְאֵין בּוֹ זְמָן,
chunks.en: or witnesses signed, but there is no date in it,
chunks.st: or there are the signatures of witnesses on the document but there is no date written in it,

chunks.en: or there is a date, but there is
chunks.st: or the date is written in it but there is only

chunks.en: only one witness,
chunks.st: the signature of a single witness.
chunks.stMore: Since there is doubt as to whether these three kinds of bills of divorce are valid, a woman who was divorced through them is only possibly divorced, and so

chunks.en: that is a doubtful get.
chunks.st: this case is called uncertainty with regard to divorce.

mishnayos.summary: A widow tied to two brothers at once (from her husband and from a maamar) cannot do yibum, because the Torah speaks of one yavam. The mishnah also repeats: a woman forbidden for one moment stays forbidden forever.

chunks.en: Three brothers married to three unrelated women,
and one of them died,
and the second made a maamar with her,

chunks.he: וָמֵת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ חוֹלְצוֹת וְלֹא מִתְיַבְּמוֹת,
chunks.en: and he died. These do chalitzah, but not yibum,
as it says (Devarim 25),

chunks.he: וּמֵת אַחַד מֵהֶם יְבָמָהּ יָבֹא עָלֶיהָ,
chunks.en: "and one of them dies… her yavam shall marry her,"

words.note: The brother who does yibum.

chunks.en: someone tied to one yavam,
and not someone tied to two yevamim.
Rabbi Shimon says,
He does yibum with whichever one he wants,
and does chalitzah with the second.
Two brothers married to two sisters,
and one of them died,

chunks.he: וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵתָה אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל שֵׁנִי,
chunks.en: and after that the second brother's wife died.
She is forbidden to him forever,
because she was forbidden to him for one moment.

mishnayos.summary: Two grooms were mixed up at their weddings, and each went home with the wrong bride. This is a serious sin, and the mishnah teaches what must be done afterward.

chunks.en: Two men made kiddushin with two women,
and when they went in to the chuppah, they switched

words.note: The wedding canopy.

chunks.en: this one's bride to that one,
and that one's bride to this one.

chunks.he: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ חַיָּבִים מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ.
chunks.en: They are guilty of the sin of a married woman.
If they were brothers,
also for a brother's wife.
And if they were sisters,
also for a woman and her sister.
And if they were niddah,

words.note: A woman who is tamei in a certain way.

chunks.en: also because of niddah.
And we keep them apart for three months,
in case they are expecting a baby.

chunks.he: וְאִם הָיוּ קְטַנּוֹת שֶׁאֵינָן רְאוּיוֹת לֵילֵד,
chunks.en: If they were young girls who cannot have children yet,
we give them back right away.
chunks.explain: Back to their real husbands.

chunks.en: And if they were from Kohen families,
they may no longer eat terumah.

words.note: A gift of food for Kohanim.

mishnayos.summary: A brother did chalitzah, and then the widow turned out to be expecting a baby. If the baby lives, the chalitzah meant nothing; if not, the chalitzah counts.

chunks.en: Someone who does chalitzah with his yevamah,
chunks.st: one who performs ḥalitza with his yevama and then

chunks.en: and she turns out to be expecting a baby, and she gives birth,
chunks.st: she is found to have been pregnant at the time of the ḥalitza and she gave birth,

chunks.en: if the baby lives,
chunks.explain: Then the dead brother has a child, so there was no yibum at all.
chunks.st: in the event that the offspring is viable, the deceased husband has been survived by offspring and so there was never any levirate bond; consequently, the ḥalitza that was performed was entirely unnecessary and a meaningless act. As such,

chunks.en: he is allowed to her relatives,
chunks.st: he remains permitted to her relatives

chunks.en: and she is allowed to his relatives,
chunks.st: and she remains permitted to his relatives.
chunks.stMore: Furthermore, since the ḥalitza was meaningless, she is not afforded the status of a ḥalutza, i.e., a yevama who performed ḥalitza, a status akin to that of a divorcée. Therefore, the ḥalitza

chunks.en: and it did not make her unfit to marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: does not disqualify her from marrying into the priesthood.

chunks.en: If the baby does not live,
chunks.st: If the offspring is not viable, then it emerges that the ḥalitza was indeed necessary. Therefore,

chunks.en: he is forbidden to her relatives,
chunks.st: he is forbidden to engage in relations with her relatives

chunks.en: and she is forbidden to his relatives,
chunks.st: and she is forbidden to engage in relations with his relatives, as though they had been married and divorced,

chunks.en: and it made her unfit to marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: and the ḥalitza disqualifies her from marrying into the priesthood, as she is afforded the status of a ḥalutza.

mishnayos.stIntro: When a man who has a brother dies childless, his widow [yevama] and one of his brothers [yavam] may perform a ritual through which she is freed of her levirate bonds [ḥalitza]. It is then considered, with regard to forbidden relationships, as though they had been married and divorced. Therefore, he is forbidden to her relatives, and she to his. However, with regard to

mishnayos.summary: A brother did yibum, and then the widow turned out to be expecting her first husband's baby. If the baby lives, the yibum was a mistake and they must separate. If it is not clear whose baby it is, they also separate.

chunks.en: Someone who marries his yevamah,
and she turns out to be expecting a baby, and she gives birth,
if the baby lives,
he must send her away, and they must bring a korban.

words.note: An animal brought to the Beis HaMikdash, here to make up for a sin.

chunks.en: And if the baby does not live,
he may keep her. If we are not sure if the baby is a nine-month baby from the first husband
or a seven-month baby from the second,
he must send her away, but the child is kosher,
chunks.explain: The child may marry anyone.

chunks.en: and they must bring an asham taluy.

words.note: A korban brought when someone is not sure if he sinned.

mishnayos.summary: A widow waiting for yibum may sell or give away property she inherited. If she dies, Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue who gets her kesubah money and her own property.

chunks.en: A woman waiting for her yavam who inherited property,

chunks.he: מוֹדִים בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל שֶׁמּוֹכֶרֶת,
chunks.en: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel agree that she may sell
and give it away, and it counts.
If she died, what do they do with her kesubah and the property

words.note: The money a husband promises his wife.

chunks.en: that comes in and goes out with her?
chunks.explain: Her own things that she brought into the marriage.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,

chunks.he: יַחֲלֹקוּ יוֹרְשֵׁי הַבַּעַל עִם יוֹרְשֵׁי הָאָב.
chunks.en: the husband's heirs split it with her father's heirs.
And Beis Hillel say,
the property stays where it was:
the kesubah stays with the husband's heirs,
and the property that comes in and goes out with her
stays with her father's heirs.

mishnayos.summary: Once the brother does yibum, she is his wife in every way, except that her kesubah is still paid from her first husband's property.

chunks.he: כְּנָסָהּ, הֲרֵי הִיא כְאִשְׁתּוֹ לְכָל דָּבָר,
chunks.en: If he married her, she is like his wife in every way,
except that her kesubah is paid from
her first husband's property.

mishnayos.summary: The oldest brother has the first mitzvah of yibum. If no brother wants to, the oldest is told: do either chalitzah or yibum.

chunks.en: The mitzvah of yibum is on the oldest brother.
If he does not want to,
they go to all the brothers.
If they do not want to,
they go back to the oldest and say to him,
"The mitzvah is on you:
either do chalitzah or do yibum."

mishnayos.summary: A brother may not make the widow wait for a younger brother to grow up, or for a brother who is far away. The beis din tells him to do chalitzah or yibum now.

chunks.en: If he wants to wait for a small brother until he grows up,

chunks.he: אוֹ בַגָּדוֹל עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא מִמְּדִינַת הַיָּם,
chunks.en: or for an older brother until he comes back from overseas,
or for a brother who cannot hear or speak,
or for one who is not in his right mind,

words.note: Someone whose mind does not work properly.

chunks.en: we do not listen to him.
Instead we say to him,
"The mitzvah is on you:
either do chalitzah or do yibum."

mishnayos.summary: The mishnah teaches who inherits the dead brother's property after chalitzah or yibum, and which relatives become forbidden after chalitzah, as if they had been married.

chunks.en: Someone who does chalitzah with his yevamah

chunks.he: הֲרֵי הוּא כְאֶחָד מִן הָאַחִין לַנַּחֲלָה.
chunks.en: is like one of the brothers for the inheritance.
And if the father is still alive,
the property belongs to the father.
Someone who does yibum with his yevamah
gets his brother's property.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
Either way,
if the father is still alive,
the property belongs to the father.
Someone who does chalitzah with his yevamah,
he is forbidden to her relatives,
and she is forbidden to his relatives.
He is forbidden to her mother,
and her mother's mother,
and her father's mother,
and her daughter, and her daughter's daughter,
and her son's daughter,
and her sister while she is still alive.
But the other brothers are allowed.
And she is forbidden to his father,
and his father's father,
and his son, and his son's son,
his brother, and his brother's son.
A man is allowed to a relative of his chalutzah's co-wife,
but forbidden to the co-wife of his chalutzah's relative.

mishnayos.summary: After a man does chalitzah with one sister, or divorces his wife, her sister is forbidden to him. So if the sister later falls to him for yibum, he cannot do yibum with her.

chunks.en: Someone who did chalitzah with his yevamah,
and his brother married her sister,
and died: she does chalitzah, but not yibum.
And so too, someone who divorced his wife,
and his brother married her sister,
and died: she is free
from chalitzah and from yibum.

mishnayos.summary: A widow is waiting for yibum, and another brother made kiddushin with her sister. He must wait to marry his bride until the widow is freed by yibum or chalitzah.

chunks.he: שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם שֶׁקִּדֵּשׁ אָחִיו אֶת אֲחוֹתָהּ,
chunks.en: A woman waiting for her yavam whose brother made kiddushin with her sister:

chunks.he: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶן בְּתֵירָא אָמְרוּ,
chunks.en: they said in the name of Rabbi Yehudah ben Beseira,
we say to him,

chunks.he: הַמְתֵּן עַד שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה אָחִיךָ הַגָּדוֹל מַעֲשֶׂה.
chunks.en: "Wait until your older brother does something."
chunks.explain: Until he does yibum or chalitzah with the widow.

chunks.en: If his brother did chalitzah with her
or married her,
he may marry his wife.
If the yevamah died,
he may marry his wife.
If the yavam died,
he must send away his wife with a get,
and his brother's wife with chalitzah.

mishnayos.summary: A widow or divorced woman must wait three months before she remarries, so we know who a new baby's father is. Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Yosei give some exceptions.

chunks.en: A yevamah may not do chalitzah or yibum
until she has waited three months.
And so too all other women
may not get engaged or married
until they have waited three months.
Both girls never married before and women married before,
both divorced women and widows,
both married women and engaged women.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
Women who were married may get engaged,
and women who were engaged may marry,
except for engaged women in Yehudah,
because the groom is very close with her.
chunks.explain: In Yehudah, the engaged couple spent time alone together.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi says,
All women may get engaged,
except for a widow,
because of her mourning.

mishnayos.summary: One brother may do yibum with several widows. When a man had two wives, yibum or chalitzah with one frees the other. Chalitzah should be done with the one who is already unfit for a Kohen.

chunks.en: Four brothers married to four women,
and they died. If the oldest of them wants
to do yibum with all of them,
he may.
Someone who was married to two women,
and died: the yibum or chalitzah of
one of them frees her co-wife.
If one was fit to marry a Kohen,
and one was unfit,
if he does chalitzah,
he does chalitzah with the unfit one.
chunks.explain: So he does not make the fit one unfit for a Kohen.

chunks.en: And if he does yibum,
he may do yibum with the fit one.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Akiva says that the child of a marriage the Torah forbids, like remarrying one's chalutzah, is a mamzer. The Sages say only a forbidden relative with a more serious punishment makes a mamzer.

chunks.en: Someone who takes back his divorced wife,
chunks.explain: After she married someone else in between.
chunks.st: With regard to one who remarries his divorcée after she had been married to another man from whom she was then widowed or divorced,

chunks.en: or marries his chalutzah,
chunks.st: or one who marries the woman with whom he performed ḥalitza [ḥalutza],

chunks.en: or marries a relative of his chalutzah,
chunks.st: or one who marries a relative of his ḥalutza, since all such marriages are forbidden he

chunks.en: must send her away, and the child is a mamzer.
chunks.st: must divorce her, and the offspring born from such unions is a mamzer; this is

words.note: A child from a forbidden marriage, who may not marry most Jews.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Akiva says.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Akiva. He holds that even the offspring from relations forbidden by a prohibition punishable by lashes is a mamzer.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: The Rabbis say:

chunks.en: the child is not a mamzer.
chunks.st: The offspring in those cases is not a mamzer,

chunks.en: But they agree about one who marries a relative of his divorced wife,
chunks.st: but they concede with regard to one who marries a relative of his divorcée, a union forbidden by a prohibition entailing karet,

chunks.en: that the child is a mamzer.
chunks.st: that the offspring is a mamzer. They hold that only the offspring from relations forbidden by a prohibition entailing karet is a mamzer.

mishnayos.summary: Who is a mamzer? Three Tannaim disagree about which forbidden marriages make a mamzer. The mishnah also teaches that once a wife or yevamah has died, her sister is allowed.

chunks.en: Who is a mamzer?
Any close relative whom the Torah forbids with "do not come,"
that is what Rabbi Akiva says.
Shimon HaTimni says,

chunks.he: כָּל שֶׁחַיָּבִין עָלָיו כָּרֵת בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם.
chunks.en: any one for whom the punishment is kareis from Heaven.

words.note: A punishment from Hashem.

chunks.en: And the halachah follows his words.
Rabbi Yehoshua says,

chunks.he: כָּל שֶׁחַיָּבִים עָלָיו מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין.
chunks.en: any one for whom beis din gives the death penalty.
Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai said,

chunks.he: מָצָאתִי מְגִלַּת יֻחֲסִין בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם וְכָתוּב בָּהּ,
chunks.en: "I found a family-record scroll in Yerushalayim, and in it was written,
'So-and-so is a mamzer from a married woman,'"
which supports what Rabbi Yehoshua says.
If his wife died,
he is allowed to marry her sister.
If he divorced her and she died,
he is allowed to her sister.
If she married another man and died,
he is allowed to her sister.
If his yevamah died,
he is allowed to her sister.
If he did chalitzah with her and she died,
he is allowed to her sister.

mishnayos.summary: If a yavam does a get, a maamar, yibum or chalitzah, can another such act still count afterward? Rabban Gamliel says no. The Sages say a get or maamar can come after another, but nothing counts after yibum or chalitzah.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says,
there is no get after a get,
and no maamar after a maamar,
and no marrying after marrying,
chunks.explain: Marrying here means finishing the yibum.

chunks.en: and no chalitzah after chalitzah.
But the Sages say,
there is a get after a get,
and there is a maamar after a maamar,
but after marrying
or after chalitzah, nothing counts.

mishnayos.summary: Examples: a yavam made a maamar and then gave a get, or made a maamar and then did chalitzah. Each time she still needs the other one. A maamar and then marrying is the proper way to do yibum.

chunks.en: How so? If he made a maamar with his yevamah
and gave her a get,
she still needs chalitzah from him.
If he made a maamar and did chalitzah,
she needs a get from him.
If he made a maamar and then married her,
that is the proper way of the mitzvah.

mishnayos.summary: More examples of doing these acts in different orders. After chalitzah, nothing else counts. These rules are the same with one yevamah or two.

chunks.en: If he gave a get and then made a maamar,
she needs a get and chalitzah.
If he gave a get and then married her,
she needs a get and chalitzah.
If he gave a get and did chalitzah,
nothing counts after chalitzah.
If he did chalitzah and then made a maamar,
or gave a get,
or married her; or if he married her and then made a maamar,
or gave a get or did chalitzah,
nothing counts after chalitzah.
It is the same with one yevamah and one yavam
and with two yevamos and one yavam.

mishnayos.summary: What happens when a yavam does different acts with two widows of the same brother. The mishnah tells which of them still needs a get or chalitzah.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד. עָשָׂה מַאֲמָר בָּזוֹ וּמַאֲמָר בָּזוֹ,
chunks.en: How so? If he made a maamar with this one and a maamar with that one,
they need two gittin and chalitzah.
A maamar with this one and a get to that one:
she needs a get and chalitzah.
A maamar with this one and married that one:
they need two gittin and chalitzah.
A maamar with this one and chalitzah with that one:
the first one needs a get.
A get to this one and a get to that one:
they need chalitzah from him.
A get to this one and married that one:
she needs a get and chalitzah.
A get to this one and a maamar with that one:
she needs a get and chalitzah.
A get to this one and chalitzah with that one:
nothing counts after chalitzah.

mishnayos.summary: After chalitzah, or after marrying the yevamah, nothing else counts, whether there is one yavam with two yevamos or two yevamin with one yevamah.

chunks.en: If he did chalitzah and chalitzah again,
or chalitzah and then a maamar,
or gave a get, or married;
or married and married again,
or married and then made a maamar,
or gave a get, or did chalitzah,
nothing counts after chalitzah.
This is true with one yavam and two yevamos
and with two yevamin and one yevamah.

mishnayos.summary: Nothing counts after chalitzah, whether it came first, in the middle, or at the end. Marrying is the same only if it came first. Rabbi Nechemyah says both are the same in every order.

chunks.en: If he did chalitzah and then a maamar,
or gave a get, or married;
or married and then made a maamar,
or gave a get, or did chalitzah,
nothing counts after chalitzah,
whether it was at the start,
whether in the middle,
whether at the end.
But marrying, if it is at the start,
nothing counts after it.
If it is in the middle or at the end,
something can still count after it.
Rabbi Nechemyah says,
both marrying and chalitzah,
whether at the start,
whether in the middle,
whether at the end,
nothing counts after it.

mishnayos.summary: Once the yavam lives with his yevamah as husband and wife, she becomes his wife, even if he did not mean to do yibum or did it by mistake.

chunks.en: Someone who lives with his yevamah as a husband,
whether by mistake,
or on purpose,
whether he was forced,
or he wanted to,
even if he made a mistake and she did it on purpose,
he on purpose and she by mistake,
he was forced and she was not forced,
she was forced and he was not forced,
whether he only began or finished,

chunks.he: קָנָה, וְלֹא חָלַק בֵּין בִּיאָה לְבִיאָה:
chunks.en: he has acquired her as his wife. And the Torah made no difference between one way and another.

mishnayos.summary: The same is true for someone who lives with a woman forbidden to him: in any way, he makes her unfit to marry a Kohen or eat terumah.

chunks.en: And so too someone who lives with one
of all the forbidden relatives in the Torah,
or women who are unfit for him,
like a widow to a Kohen Gadol,
a divorced woman or a chalutzah to a regular Kohen,
a mamzeres or a Nesinah to a Jew,
a Jewish girl to a mamzer or a Nasin,

chunks.he: פָּסַל. וְלֹא חָלַק בֵּין בִּיאָה לְבִיאָה:
chunks.en: he makes her unfit. And the Torah made no difference between one way and another.

mishnayos.summary: A widow engaged to a Kohen Gadol, or a divorced woman engaged to a regular Kohen, may not eat terumah. Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Shimon allow it. If the engagement ends, she is fit again.

chunks.en: A widow to a Kohen Gadol,
a divorced woman or a chalutzah to a regular Kohen,
from the time of engagement may not eat terumah.
chunks.explain: Even if they are daughters of Kohanim.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Shimon say they are fit.
If they were widowed or divorced,
after marriage they are unfit,
after engagement they are fit.

mishnayos.summary: A Kohen Gadol may marry only a young girl who was never married. If he was engaged to a widow before becoming Kohen Gadol, he may still marry her, as Yehoshua ben Gamla did.

chunks.en: A Kohen Gadol may not marry a widow,
whether a widow after engagement
or a widow after marriage.
And he may not marry a grown-up girl.

words.note: A girl who is fully grown, older than twelve and a half.

chunks.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַכְשִׁירִין בְּבוֹגֶרֶת.
chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Shimon say a bogeres is fit.
He may not marry a girl hurt in an accident.
chunks.explain: An accident made her no longer counted as a besulah.

chunks.en: If he was engaged to a widow,
and then he was made Kohen Gadol,

chunks.he: יִכְנֹס. וּמַעֲשֶׂה בִיהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן גַּמְלָא שֶׁקִּדֵּשׁ
chunks.en: he may marry her. It once happened that Yehoshua ben Gamla made kiddushin with
Marta bas Baysos,
and the king made him Kohen Gadol,

chunks.he: וּכְנָסָהּ. שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם שֶׁנָּפְלָה לִפְנֵי כֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט,
chunks.en: and he married her. A widow waiting for yibum who fell to a regular Kohen,
and then he was made Kohen Gadol,

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעָשָׂה בָהּ מַאֲמָר,
chunks.en: even though he made a maamar with her,
may not marry her.
A Kohen Gadol whose brother died
does chalitzah, not yibum.

mishnayos.summary: A regular Kohen should not marry a woman who cannot have children, unless he already has children. Rabbi Yehudah and the Sages argue about who counts as a zonah.

chunks.en: A regular Kohen may not marry an aylonis,

words.note: A woman who cannot have children.

chunks.en: unless
he has a wife and children.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
Even if
he has a wife and children,
he may not marry an aylonis,
because she is the zonah the Torah speaks about.

words.note: A woman a Kohen may not marry.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
a zonah is only a woman who became a Jew,
a freed maidservant, and one who was with a man in a forbidden way.

mishnayos.summary: Every man must have children. Beis Shammai say two boys; Beis Hillel say a boy and a girl. The mishnah also argues whether a woman has this mitzvah too.

chunks.en: A man may not stop the mitzvah of having children,
chunks.st: A man may not neglect the mitzva to be fruitful and multiply

chunks.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֶשׁ לוֹ בָנִים.
chunks.en: unless he already has children.
chunks.st: unless he already has children.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say: One fulfills this mitzva with

chunks.en: two boys.
chunks.st: two males,

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: a boy and a girl,
chunks.st: A male and a female,

chunks.en: as it says (Bereishis 5), "Male and female He created them."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Male and female He created them” (Genesis 5:2). If a man

chunks.en: If he married a woman
chunks.st: married a woman

chunks.en: and stayed with her ten years,
chunks.st: and stayed with her for ten years

chunks.en: and she did not have a child,
chunks.st: and she did not give birth,

chunks.en: he may not stop trying to have children.
chunks.st: he is no longer permitted to neglect the mitzva to be fruitful and multiply.
chunks.stMore: Consequently, he must either divorce her and marry someone else, or take another wife while still married to her. If

chunks.en: If he divorced her, she may marry another man,
chunks.st: he divorced her she is permitted to marry another man, as it is not necessarily on her account that she and her first husband did not have children,

chunks.he: וְרַשַּׁאי הַשֵּׁנִי לִשְׁהוֹת עִמָּהּ עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים.
chunks.en: and the second husband may stay with her ten years.
chunks.st: and the second husband is permitted to stay with her for ten years.

chunks.en: And if she lost a baby before it was born,
chunks.st: And if she had a miscarriage,

chunks.en: he counts from when she lost it.
chunks.st: he counts the ten years from the time of the miscarriage.

chunks.en: A man has the mitzvah to have children,
chunks.st: A man is commanded with regard to the mitzva to be fruitful and multiply,

chunks.en: but not a woman.
chunks.st: but not a woman.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Berokah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says that a woman is also commanded, as the verse

chunks.en: about both of them it says (Bereishis 1),
chunks.st: states with regard to both of them: “

chunks.en: "And Hashem blessed them, and He said
chunks.st: And God blessed them, and God said

chunks.en: to them, 'Be fruitful and multiply.'"
chunks.st: to them: Be fruitful and multiply” (Genesis 1:28).

mishnayos.summary: When a woman forbidden to her Kohen husband brings slaves into the marriage, it depends on whose they really are: slaves that stay hers may not eat terumah, but slaves that belong to him may.

chunks.en: A widow married to a Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: A widow married to a High Priest, and

chunks.en: a divorced woman or a chalutzah married to a regular Kohen,
chunks.st: a divorcée or a yevama who performed ḥalitza [ḥalutza] married to a common priest are all unions prohibited by Torah law. If one of these women

chunks.en: if she brought him "melog" slaves
chunks.st: brought with her into the marriage slaves of usufruct [melog] property

words.note: Her own property, which the husband may only use.

chunks.en: and "tzon barzel" slaves,
chunks.st: or slaves of guaranteed investment, then the

words.note: Property the husband takes over and promises to pay back.

chunks.en: the melog slaves may not eat terumah,
chunks.st: slaves of usufruct property do not partake of teruma but the

chunks.en: but the tzon barzel slaves may eat.
chunks.st: slaves of guaranteed investment do partake of teruma.

chunks.en: These are melog slaves:
chunks.st: And these are slaves of usufruct property:

chunks.en: if they die,
chunks.st: They are those with regard to whom the couple stipulated that if the slaves die,

chunks.en: they die as her loss,
chunks.st: their death is her loss,

chunks.en: and if they go up in value,
chunks.st: and if they increase in value,

chunks.en: they go up for her.
chunks.st: their increase is her gain.

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא חַיָּב בִּמְזוֹנוֹתָן,
chunks.en: Even though he must feed them,
chunks.st: Although the husband is obligated in their sustenance,

chunks.en: they may not eat terumah.
chunks.st: they do not partake of teruma, as they belong to her, not to him. He owns only the right of their use while he is married to her.

chunks.en: These are tzon barzel slaves:
chunks.st: And these are slaves of guaranteed investment: They are those with regard to whom the couple stipulated that

chunks.en: if they die,
chunks.st: if they die, their

chunks.en: they die as his loss,
chunks.st: death is his loss,

chunks.en: and if they go up in value,
chunks.st: and if they increase in value, their increase is his

chunks.en: they go up for him.
chunks.st: gain.

chunks.en: Since he is responsible for them,
chunks.st: Since he bears financial responsibility for compensating her in the event of their loss,

chunks.en: they may eat terumah.
chunks.st: they partake of teruma, as they are considered his property.

mishnayos.summary: When a regular Jewish woman marries a Kohen, all the slaves she brings may eat terumah. When a Kohen's daughter marries a regular Jew, her slaves may not.

chunks.en: A Jewish woman who married a Kohen
chunks.st: In the case of an Israelite woman who married a priest in a halakhic marriage

chunks.en: and brought slaves into the marriage,
chunks.st: and who brought slaves with her into the marriage,

chunks.en: whether melog slaves
chunks.st: whether they are slaves of usufruct property

chunks.en: or tzon barzel slaves,
chunks.st: or slaves of guaranteed investment, they

chunks.en: they may eat terumah.
chunks.st: partake of teruma. And

chunks.en: And a Kohen's daughter who married a regular Jew
chunks.st: in the case of the daughter of a priest who married an Israelite

chunks.en: and brought slaves into the marriage,
chunks.st: and who brought slaves with her into the marriage,

chunks.en: whether melog slaves
chunks.st: whether they are slaves of usufruct property

chunks.en: or tzon barzel slaves,
chunks.st: or slaves of guaranteed investment, they

chunks.en: they may not eat terumah.
chunks.st: do not partake of teruma, although, as she is the daughter of a priest, it is permitted for her and her slaves to partake of teruma beforehand.

mishnayos.summary: A Kohen died and his wife is expecting a baby. Rabbi Yosei says her slaves may not eat terumah, because the unborn baby owns part of them. The Sages say this is true even if she is a Kohen's daughter.

chunks.en: A Jewish woman who married a Kohen,
chunks.st: With regard to an Israelite woman who married a priest

chunks.en: and he died and left her expecting a baby,
chunks.st: and he died and left her pregnant,

chunks.en: her slaves may not eat terumah,
chunks.st: her slaves of guaranteed investment may not partake of teruma during her pregnancy,

chunks.en: because of the unborn baby's share,
chunks.explain: The baby will inherit part of the slaves.
chunks.st: due to the share of the fetus, as an inheritor of his father, in the ownership of the slaves. In the opposite case,

chunks.en: because an unborn baby can make unfit, but cannot let someone eat.
chunks.st: where the Israelite husband of a priest’s daughter died and left her pregnant, the fetus disqualifies her from partaking of teruma. However, in the current case, the fetus does not enable its mother or the slaves to partake of teruma, despite the fact that it is the child of a priest. This is

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Yosi says.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Yosei. The Rabbis

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: said to him:

chunks.en: "Since you told us about
chunks.st: Since you testified before us about the case of

chunks.en: a Jewish woman married to a Kohen,
chunks.st: an Israelite woman who was married to a priest, in the case of

chunks.en: then also a Kohen's daughter married to a Kohen,
chunks.st: the daughter of a priest who was married to a priest

chunks.en: who died and left her expecting a baby,
chunks.st: and he died and left her pregnant,

chunks.en: her slaves may not eat terumah,
chunks.st: her slaves should not partake of teruma either,

chunks.en: because of the unborn baby's share."
chunks.st: due to the fetus’s share. The same halakha should apply whether the woman is an Israelite or the daughter of a priest.

mishnayos.summary: Some people can make a Kohen's daughter unfit to eat terumah, but cannot let a regular Jewish woman eat it. The mishnah also teaches what happens when a house falls on a man and his wife together.

chunks.en: An unborn baby, a yavam,
an engagement, and a deaf-mute,
and a boy nine years and one day old,
make unfit, but do not let her eat.
chunks.explain: A Kohen's daughter may not eat because of them, but they cannot let other women eat.

chunks.en: If we are not sure whether he is nine years
and one day old or not,
if we are not sure whether he has two hairs

words.note: A sign that a boy is grown up.

chunks.en: or not, they also make unfit.

chunks.he: נָפַל הַבַּיִת עָלָיו וְעַל בַּת אָחִיו
chunks.en: If a house fell on him and on his brother's daughter, his wife,

chunks.he: וְאֵין יָדוּעַ אֵי זֶה מֵת רִאשׁוֹן,
chunks.en: and we do not know which one died first,
her co-wife does chalitzah, but not yibum.

mishnayos.summary: More people who can or cannot make a woman unfit for terumah. Sometimes a child lets his mother eat terumah when his father could not. A slave or a mamzer grandchild can also change whether a grandmother may eat terumah.

chunks.en: A man who forced a girl, or tricked her,
chunks.explain: He was with her without marrying her.

chunks.en: and a shoteh, do not make unfit and do not let eat.
But if they may not marry into the Jewish people,
they do make unfit.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד, יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבָּא עַל בַּת כֹּהֵן,
chunks.en: How so? A regular Jew who was with a Kohen's daughter
she may still eat terumah.
If she is expecting a baby, she may not eat terumah.
If the baby was lost before birth,

chunks.he: תֹּאכַל. כֹּהֵן שֶׁבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: she may eat. A Kohen who was with a regular Jewish woman,
she may not eat terumah.
If she is expecting a baby, she may not eat.
If she gave birth, she may eat.
So the power of the son
is greater than the father's.
A slave makes unfit by being with her,
but not by being her descendant.
How so? A Jewish woman married to a Kohen,
or a Kohen's daughter married to a regular Jew,
and she had a son from him,
and the son went and was with a maidservant,
and she had a son from him,
that son is a slave.
If his father's mother was a Jewish woman
married to a Kohen, she may not eat terumah.
If she was a Kohen's daughter married to a regular Jew,
she may eat terumah.
A mamzer makes unfit and lets eat.
How so? A Jewish woman married to a Kohen,
or a Kohen's daughter married to a regular Jew,
and she had a daughter from him,
and the daughter went and married a slave
or a non-Jew,
and had a son from him,
that son is a mamzer.

chunks.he: הָיְתָה אֵם אִמּוֹ בַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכֹהֵן,
chunks.en: If his mother's mother was a Jewish woman married to a Kohen,
she may eat terumah.
If she was a Kohen's daughter married to a regular Jew,
she may not eat terumah.

mishnayos.summary: Sometimes even a grandson who could be the Kohen Gadol makes his grandmother unfit to eat terumah, so she says, "I hope there are not many like my grandson!"

chunks.en: A Kohen Gadol sometimes makes unfit.
chunks.st: Even with regard to a High Priest, sometimes he disqualifies his grandmother from partaking of teruma.

chunks.st: How so? If the daughter of a priest was married to an Israelite,

mishnayos.summary: A Kohen who is tamei or who did not have a bris may not eat terumah, but his wife and slaves may. A Kohen with a certain injury may eat terumah, but his wife may not, unless the injury came after they were together as husband and wife.

chunks.en: An uncircumcised Kohen and all who are tamei

words.note: A Kohen who could not have a bris because it was dangerous.

chunks.en: may not eat terumah.
Their wives and their slaves
may eat terumah.
A man with a certain injury, or another kind of such injury,
chunks.explain: Injuries that keep a man from having children.

chunks.en: they and their slaves may eat,
but their wives may not eat.
And if he was not with her as a husband since he became
injured in this way,
she may eat.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah explains which injuries count for the last mishnah. Such a man may not marry a girl born Jewish, but he may marry a convert or a freed maidservant.

chunks.en: Who counts as "injured" (petzua daka)?
Anyone whose body was injured there,
even only one of them.
And who counts as "cut" (kerus shafchah)?
Anyone whose body part was cut off.

chunks.he: וְאִם נִשְׁתַּיֵּר מֵהָעֲטָרָה אֲפִלּוּ כְּחוּט הַשַּׂעֲרָה,
chunks.en: And if even a hair's width is left of it,
he is fit. Petzua daka and kerus shafchah
may marry a convert or a freed maidservant.
They are only forbidden to marry into the Jewish people,
as it says (Devarim 23),
"A man with these injuries
shall not come into the congregation of Hashem."

chunks.en: An Amoni and a Moavi
chunks.st: Ammonite and Moabite converts

chunks.en: are forbidden, and forever,

chunks.st: are prohibited from entering into the congregation and marrying a woman who was born Jewish, and their prohibition is eternal, for all generations.

chunks.en: but their women are allowed right away.
chunks.st: However, their female counterparts, even the convert herself, are permitted immediately.

chunks.en: A Mitzri and an Edomi are forbidden

chunks.en: are forbidden, and forever,
