mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yehoshua heard two rulings about a man who cannot have children, one saying he does chalitzah and one saying he does not. Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Eliezer explain them in opposite ways.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said,
"I heard that a saris does chalitzah,

words.note: A man who cannot have children.

chunks.en: and they do chalitzah with his wife,

chunks.he: וְהַסָּרִיס לֹא חוֹלֵץ וְלֹא חוֹלְצִין לְאִשְׁתּוֹ,
chunks.en: and that a saris does not do chalitzah, and they do not do chalitzah with his wife,
and I cannot explain it."
Rabbi Akiva said,
"I will explain.
A saris made by people does chalitzah, and they do chalitzah with his wife,
chunks.explain: He was hurt after he was born.

chunks.en: because he had a time when he was fit.
A saris from birth does not do chalitzah
chunks.explain: He was born this way.

chunks.en: and they do not do chalitzah with his wife,

chunks.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁעַת הַכֹּשֶׁר.
chunks.en: because he never had a time when he was fit."
Rabbi Eliezer says,
"Not so.
Rather, a saris from birth does chalitzah,
and they do chalitzah with his wife,
because he can be healed.
A saris made by people does not do chalitzah
and they do not do chalitzah with his wife,
because he cannot be healed."

chunks.he: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן בְּתֵירָא עַל
chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Beseira told about

chunks.he: בֶּן מְגוּסַת שֶׁהָיָה בִירוּשָׁלַיִם סְרִיס אָדָם,
chunks.en: ben Megusas in Yerushalayim, a saris made by people,
that they did yibum with his wife,
which supports what Rabbi Akiva says.

mishnayos.summary: A man or woman who cannot have children does not do yibum or chalitzah. If they did chalitzah anyway, it does not make her unfit, but marrying her does.

chunks.en: A saris does not do chalitzah or yibum.

chunks.he: וְכֵן אַיְלוֹנִית לֹא חוֹלֶצֶת וְלֹא מִתְיַבֶּמֶת.
chunks.en: And so an aylonis does not do chalitzah or yibum.
A saris who did chalitzah with his yevamah
did not make her unfit.
If he married her, he made her unfit,
because it was a forbidden marriage.
And so an aylonis who did chalitzah with the brothers
was not made unfit.
If they married her, they made her unfit,
because it was a forbidden marriage.

mishnayos.summary: Some unusual cases: a Kohen who cannot have children, or an androginos Kohen, may let his wife eat terumah. The mishnah also discusses a tumtum and an androginos.

chunks.he: סְרִיס חַמָּה כֹּהֵן שֶׁנָּשָׂא בַת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: A Kohen who was a saris from birth and married a Jewish woman
lets her eat terumah.
Rabbi Yosi and Rabbi Shimon say,
an androginos Kohen who married a Jewish woman

words.note: Someone with signs of both a man and a woman.

chunks.en: lets her eat terumah.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
a tumtum who was opened and found to be a male

words.note: Someone whose body does not show if he is a boy or a girl.

chunks.en: may not do chalitzah,
because he is like a saris.
An androginos may marry a woman,
but may not be married to a man.
Rabbi Eliezer says,
an androginos counts like a male, and sinning with him is punished with stoning.

mishnayos.summary: Some widows were allowed to their husbands but are forbidden to the brother who would do yibum, because of who he is. The mishnah gives examples, like a widow whose brother-in-law is the Kohen Gadol.

chunks.en: Some women are allowed to their husbands but forbidden to their yevamin,
some are allowed to their yevamin but forbidden to their husbands,
some are allowed to both,
and some are forbidden to both.
These are allowed to their husbands but forbidden to their yevamin:
A regular Kohen who married a widow
and has a brother who is Kohen Gadol,
a chalal who married a woman fit for a Kohen

words.note: A son of a Kohen born from a marriage forbidden to Kohanim; he is not a full Kohen.

chunks.en: and has a brother who is a fit Kohen,
a regular Jew who married a Jewish woman
and has a brother who is a mamzer,
a mamzer who married a mamzeres
and has a brother who is a regular Jew:
these are allowed to their husbands but forbidden to their yevamin.

mishnayos.summary: Other women are forbidden to their husbands but allowed to the yavam, and some are forbidden to both. All other women are allowed to both.

chunks.en: And these are allowed to their yevamin but forbidden to their husbands:
A Kohen Gadol who made kiddushin with a widow
and has a brother who is a regular Kohen,
a fit Kohen who married a chalalah

words.note: A woman who became unfit to marry a Kohen.

chunks.en: and has a brother who is a chalal,
a regular Jew who married a mamzeres
and has a brother who is a mamzer,
a mamzer who married a Jewish woman
and has a brother who is a regular Jew:
these are allowed to their yevamin but forbidden to their husbands.
Forbidden to both:
a Kohen Gadol who married a widow
and has a brother who is Kohen Gadol
or a regular Kohen,
a fit Kohen who married a chalalah
and has a brother who is a fit Kohen,
a regular Jew who married a mamzeres
and has a brother who is a regular Jew,
a mamzer who married a Jewish woman
and has a brother who is a mamzer:
these are forbidden to both.
And all other women
are allowed to their husbands and to their yevamin.

mishnayos.summary: People wrongly told a woman her husband died overseas, so she remarried. When her first husband comes back, she must leave both men and loses many rights. Other Tannaim give some of the rules differently.

chunks.en: A woman whose husband went overseas,
and people came and told her,
"Your husband died,"
and she married someone else, and then her husband came back,
she must leave both of them,
and she needs a get from both of them.
She gets no kesubah, no payment for fruits,
no food, and no worn-out things,

chunks.he: לֹא עַל זֶה וְלֹא עַל זֶה.
chunks.en: not from this one and not from that one.
If she took them from either one,
she must give them back. And the child is a mamzer from either one.
Neither of them may become tamei for her if she dies,
chunks.explain: A Kohen may become tamei to bury his wife, but not here.

chunks.en: and neither of them gets
the things she finds, or what she earns,
or the right to cancel her nedarim.
If she was a Jewish woman,
she becomes unfit to marry a Kohen;
a Levi's daughter becomes unfit to eat ma'aser,
and a Kohen's daughter unfit to eat terumah.
And the heirs of this one and the heirs
of that one do not inherit her kesubah.
And if they died,
the brothers of this one and the brothers of
that one do chalitzah, but not yibum.
Rabbi Yosi says,
her kesubah is paid from her first husband's property.
Rabbi Elazar says,
The first one gets what she finds and what she earns,
and may cancel her nedarim.
And Rabbi Shimon says,
her yibum or chalitzah with the brother
of the first husband frees her co-wife,
and a child from him is not a mamzer.
And if she married without permission,
chunks.explain: Without asking a beis din.

chunks.en: she may go back to him.

mishnayos.summary: If she remarried because beis din allowed it, she does not need to bring a korban. If she remarried on her own, she must bring one.

chunks.en: If she married by permission of beis din,
she must leave, but she does not bring a korban.

chunks.he: לֹא נִסֵּת עַל פִּי בֵית דִּין,
chunks.en: If she did not marry by permission of beis din,
she must leave, and she must bring a korban.
The power of beis din is great,
since it frees her from the korban.
If beis din told her she may marry,
and she went and did wrong,
she must bring a korban,
because they only allowed her to marry.

mishnayos.summary: Wrong reports about whether her husband or her son died first can change whether she needed yibum. If the report was wrong, her marriage was forbidden and she must leave.

chunks.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלַךְ בַּעֲלָהּ וּבְנָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם,
chunks.en: A woman whose husband and son went overseas,
chunks.st: With regard to a woman whose husband and child went overseas, and witnesses

chunks.en: and people came and told her,
chunks.st: came and said to her:

chunks.he: מֵת בַּעְלֵךְ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת בְּנֵךְ,
chunks.en: "Your husband died, and after that your son died,"
chunks.explain: Then she had a child when her husband died, so no yibum was needed.
chunks.st: Your husband died and afterward your child died, she does not require levirate marriage, as she had a child when her husband died.

chunks.en: and she married. Then they told her,
chunks.st: And for this reason she married another man. And if afterward they said to her that

chunks.en: "It was the other way around,"
chunks.st: the matters were reversed, i.e., the child died before the husband, which means that she did require levirate marriage, she is therefore a yevama who married a stranger without ḥalitza and

chunks.en: she must leave, and the first and last children are mamzerim.
chunks.st: she must consequently leave her second husband. And with regard to the first child, the one born before they heard about the reversal, and the last one, born after they realized who actually died first, each of these children is a mamzer.

chunks.en: If they told her,
chunks.st: Conversely, if they said to her:

chunks.he: מֵת בְּנֵךְ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת בַּעְלֵךְ,
chunks.en: "Your son died, and after that your husband died,"
chunks.st: Your child died and afterward your husband died,

chunks.en: and she did yibum, and then they told her,
chunks.st: and she therefore entered into levirate marriage, and afterward they said to her that

chunks.en: "It was the other way around,"
chunks.st: the matters were reversed, which means she married her husband’s brother when there was no obligation of levirate marriage,

chunks.en: she must leave, and the first and last children are mamzerim.
chunks.st: she must leave her husband, and the first child and the last one are each a mamzer.

chunks.en: If they told her,
chunks.st: If they said to her:

chunks.en: "Your husband died,"
chunks.st: Your husband died,

chunks.en: and she married, and then they told her,
chunks.st: and she married, and afterward they said to her that

chunks.en: "He was alive then, and died later,"
chunks.st: he was alive at the time of her marriage and he later died,

chunks.en: she must leave, and the first child is a mamzer,
chunks.st: she must leave the second husband. And the first child, born when her original husband was still alive, is a mamzer,

chunks.en: but the last one is not a mamzer.
chunks.st: and the last one, born after his death, is not a mamzer.

chunks.en: If they told her,
chunks.st: If they said to her:

chunks.en: "Your husband died,"
chunks.st: Your husband died,

chunks.en: and she got engaged, and then her husband came back,
chunks.st: and she became betrothed to another man, and afterward her husband came,

chunks.en: she may go back to him.
chunks.st: she is permitted to return to him, as betrothal alone does not render her forbidden to her husband.

chunks.en: Even though
chunks.st: Furthermore, although the

chunks.en: the second man gave her a get,
chunks.st: last man, i.e., her betrothed, gave her a bill of divorce,

chunks.en: he did not make her unfit to marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: he has not thereby disqualified her from marrying into the priesthood.
chunks.stMore: She was never his wife, for the betrothal was invalid, and a bill of divorce given to the wife of another man does not disqualify her.

chunks.st: Elazar ben Matya: The verse states with regard to priests: “

chunks.st: Neither shall they take a woman divorced from her husband” (Leviticus 21:7), which indicates:

chunks.en: and not from a man who is not her husband.
chunks.st: And not one who was divorced from a man who is not her husband, e.g., the second man in this case.

mishnayos.summary: A man was wrongly told that his wife died, and he married her sister. When his wife comes back, she may return to him. The mishnah also tells which children are mamzerim.

chunks.en: A man whose wife went overseas,
and people came and told him,
"Your wife died,"
and he married her sister,
and then his wife came back,
she may go back to him.
He is allowed to the second one's relatives,
and the second is allowed to his relatives.
And if the first one died,
he may marry the second.
If they told him,
"Your wife died,"
and he married her sister,
and then they told him,
"She was alive then,
and died later," the first child is a mamzer,
and the last one is not a mamzer.
Rabbi Yosi says,
Whoever makes unfit through others
makes unfit through himself,

chunks.he: וְכָל שֶׁאֵין פּוֹסֵל עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים,
chunks.en: and whoever does not make unfit through others
does not make unfit through himself.

mishnayos.summary: A man was told again and again that his wife died, and each time he married her sister. When they all turn out to be alive, only some of the marriages count. The mishnah tells which ones.

chunks.en: They told him,
"Your wife died,"
and he married her sister from her father.
She died, and he married her sister from her mother.
She died, and he married her sister from her father.
She died, and he married her sister from her mother.
And they all turned out to be alive.
He is allowed to the first,
the third, and the fifth,
chunks.explain: These are not sisters of each other, so these marriages count.

chunks.en: and they free their co-wives,
and he is forbidden to the second and the fourth,

chunks.he: וְאֵין בִּיאַת אַחַת מֵהֶן פּוֹטֶרֶת צָרָתָהּ.
chunks.en: and yibum with one of them does not free her co-wife.
And if he married the second
after the first one really died,
he is allowed to the second and the fourth,
and they free their co-wives,
and he is forbidden to the third and the fifth,

chunks.he: וְאֵין בִּיאַת אַחַת מֵהֶן פּוֹטֶרֶת צָרָתָהּ:
chunks.en: and yibum with one of them does not free her co-wife.

mishnayos.summary: A boy nine years and one day old who does yibum is not like a grown-up, but what he does still counts in some ways. His brothers' acts can block him even if they come later.

chunks.en: A boy nine years and one day old
makes her unfit for the brothers,
and the brothers make her unfit for him.
But he makes unfit only if he is first,
and the brothers make unfit whether first or last.
How so? A boy nine years and one
day old who did yibum with his yevamah
made her unfit for the brothers.
If the brothers did yibum with her,
or made a maamar with her,
or gave a get, or did chalitzah,
they made her unfit for him.

mishnayos.summary: If two young brothers, each nine years and one day old, both did yibum with the same widow, the second one makes her unfit for the first. Rabbi Shimon disagrees.

chunks.en: A boy nine years and one
day old who did yibum with his yevamah,

chunks.he: וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּא עָלֶיהָ אָחִיו שֶׁהוּא
chunks.en: and after that his brother, who is also
nine years and one day old, did yibum with her,
he makes her unfit for him.
Rabbi Shimon says,
he does not make her unfit.

mishnayos.summary: A boy nine years and one day old who did yibum with one widow and then with her co-wife makes them unfit for himself. Rabbi Shimon disagrees. If he dies, his yevamah does chalitzah, and a wife he married is free.

chunks.en: A boy nine years and one
day old who did yibum with his yevamah,
and after that with her co-wife,
made them unfit for himself.
Rabbi Shimon says,
he did not make them unfit.
A boy nine years and one
day old who did yibum with his yevamah
and then died: she does chalitzah, but not yibum.
If he married a woman and died,
she is free.
chunks.explain: A young boy's marriage does not count from the Torah.

mishnayos.summary: A boy did yibum when he was nine, and when he grew up he married another woman and died. The first widow does only chalitzah, but the second may do yibum. The same is true for an older man who still has not shown signs of growing up.

chunks.en: A boy nine years and one
day old who did yibum with his yevamah,
and after he grew up he married another woman and died.

chunks.he: אִם לֹא יָדַע אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה מִשֶּׁהִגְדִּיל,
chunks.en: If he did not live with the first one after he grew up,
the first does chalitzah, but not yibum,
and the second either does chalitzah or yibum.
Rabbi Shimon says,
He does yibum with whichever he wants,
and does chalitzah with the other.
The same is true for one who is nine
years and one day old,
and for one who is twenty years old
who has not shown two hairs.
chunks.explain: Two hairs are a sign of growing up.

mishnayos.summary: A man who wronged a woman without marrying her may still marry her relatives, but not the relatives of his wife. Rabbi Yehudah adds a case that he forbids.

chunks.en: One may marry the relative of a woman who was forced or tricked.
chunks.explain: These women were wronged by a man who did not marry them.

chunks.en: But one who forces or tricks a relative of his wife

chunks.he: חַיָּב. נוֹשֵׂא אָדָם אֲנוּסַת אָבִיו וּמְפֻתַּת אָבִיו,
chunks.en: is guilty. A man may marry a woman his father forced or tricked,
or one his son forced or tricked.
Rabbi Yehudah forbids a woman forced
or tricked by his father.

mishnayos.summary: When a woman becomes a Jew together with her sons, the sons do not count as brothers for yibum or chalitzah. The same is true for a freed maidservant and her sons.

chunks.en: A convert woman whose sons became Jews with her
chunks.st: With regard to a female convert whose sons converted with her,

chunks.en: they do not do chalitzah or yibum,
chunks.explain: Becoming a Jew is like being born again, so they are not counted as brothers.
chunks.st: they do not perform ḥalitza for each other’s wives, and they do not perform levirate marriage with them, as their conversions are considered rebirth, and they are considered unrelated. This is so

chunks.en: even if the first son was conceived
chunks.st: even if the conception of the first son

chunks.en: before she became a Jew and born after,
chunks.st: was not in the sanctity of Israel, i.e., the mother had not yet converted when she conceived of him, but his birth was in the sanctity of Israel, as his mother had converted by the time she gave birth to him,

chunks.en: and the second was conceived and born after.
chunks.st: whereas the second son was both conceived and born in sanctity. The first son is considered a convert, who is unrelated to his brother.

chunks.en: And the same is true for a maidservant whose sons were freed with her.
chunks.st: And this halakha similarly applies to a maidservant whose sons were freed with her, as they too are not considered relatives.

mishnayos.summary: Five mothers' babies got mixed up, so nobody knows which boy belongs to which mother. When they grew up, married and died, each widow needs chalitzah from four brothers and then may do yibum with the fifth.

chunks.en: Five women whose babies got mixed up,
chunks.st: With regard to five women whose offspring were mixed, i.e., their lineage became indeterminate, and they had other sons as well who were not mixed,

chunks.en: and the mixed-up boys grew up, married women, and died.
chunks.st: and the mixed sons matured and married women and subsequently died,

chunks.en: Four brothers do chalitzah with one widow,
chunks.explain: Each from a different mother, so one of them must be her real brother-in-law.
chunks.st: then four sons who were not mixed, each one from a different mother, must perform ḥalitza with one of the widows, as she might be the sister-in-law of any of them.

chunks.en: and one does yibum with her.
chunks.st: And one son of the mother whose sons did not perform ḥalitza may perform levirate marriage with her instead of ḥalitza; even if she is not his sister-in-law, once she has received ḥalitza from the others she may marry any man.

chunks.en: He and three others do chalitzah with another widow,
chunks.st: Subsequently, he and three of the four other sons must perform ḥalitza with one of the remaining widows,

chunks.en: and one does yibum.
chunks.st: and the other one may perform levirate marriage.

chunks.en: So there are four chalitzos and one yibum
chunks.st: When this process has been completed for all the widows, four ḥalitzot and a levirate marriage are found altogether

chunks.en: for each and every one.
chunks.st: for each and every widow.

mishnayos.summary: A grandmother's baby was mixed up with her daughter-in-law's baby. So one is the other's uncle, but no one knows which. The mishnah teaches who may do yibum and who only chalitzah.

chunks.en: A woman whose baby got mixed up with her daughter-in-law's baby
chunks.st: With regard to a woman whose offspring was mixed with the offspring of her daughter-in-law, and their lineage was consequently indeterminate,

chunks.en: the mixed-up boys grew up,
chunks.st: and the mixed sons matured and

chunks.en: married women,
chunks.st: married women, and subsequently

chunks.he: וּמֵתוּ, בְּנֵי הַכַּלָּה חוֹלְצִין וְלֹא מְיַבְּמִין,
chunks.en: and died. The daughter-in-law's sons do chalitzah, but not yibum,
chunks.st: they died, the certain sons of the daughter-in-law perform ḥalitza with the wives, but not levirate marriage,

chunks.en: because she may be his brother's wife
chunks.st: as with regard to each wife it is uncertain whether she is his brother’s wife, and therefore his yevama, and

chunks.en: or his uncle's wife.
chunks.st: uncertain whether she is his father’s brother’s wife, who is forbidden to him.

chunks.en: And the grandmother's sons
chunks.st: However, the certain sons of the elder woman, i.e., the mother-in-law,

chunks.en: may either do chalitzah or yibum,
chunks.st: perform either ḥalitza or levirate marriage,

chunks.en: because she is either his brother's wife
chunks.st: as with regard to each wife it is uncertain whether she is his brother’s wife, in which case levirate marriage is valid,

chunks.en: or his nephew's wife.
chunks.st: or his brother’s son’s wife, in which case she is permitted to him, after having performed ḥalitza with a son of the daughter-in-law.

chunks.en: If the sure sons died,
chunks.st: If the sons of certain, unflawed lineage were the ones who died, then

chunks.en: the mixed-up sons, with the grandmother's sons' widows,
chunks.st: the mixed sons perform

chunks.en: do chalitzah, but not yibum,
chunks.st: ḥalitza with the widows of the elder woman’s sons but not levirate marriage,

chunks.en: because she may be his brother's wife
chunks.st: as it is uncertain whether she is his brother’s wife

chunks.en: or his uncle's wife.
chunks.st: or his father’s brother’s wife.

chunks.en: And with the daughter-in-law's sons' widows,
chunks.st: With the widows of the certain sons of the daughter-in-law,

chunks.en: one does chalitzah and one does yibum.
chunks.st: one of the mixed sons performs ḥalitza, in case she is his brother’s wife. And the other one performs levirate marriage, as even if she is his brother’s son’s wife, she is permitted to him.

mishnayos.summary: A Kohen's wife's baby got mixed up with her maidservant's baby. Since each boy may be a Kohen or a slave, they get the strict rules of both, as the mishnah lists.

chunks.en: A Kohen's wife whose baby got mixed up with her maidservant's baby:
chunks.st: In the case of a priestess whose offspring was mixed with her maidservant’s offspring,

chunks.en: they may eat terumah,
chunks.explain: A Kohen's slave may also eat terumah.
chunks.st: they may partake of teruma, as both a priest and the slave of a priest partake of teruma.

chunks.en: and they get one share at the threshing floor.
chunks.st: And they receive one share of teruma in the granary.

chunks.en: They may not become tamei from the dead,
chunks.st: And they may not become ritually impure with impurity imparted by a corpse, as each of them might be a priest.

chunks.en: and they may not marry women,
chunks.st: And they may not marry women,

chunks.en: whether fit or unfit.
chunks.st: whether unflawed women, who may not marry a slave, or women unfit to marry into the priesthood, as with regard to each of them it is uncertain whether he is a priest or a slave.

chunks.en: If the mixed-up boys grew up
chunks.st: If the mixed sons matured

chunks.en: and freed each other,
chunks.st: and freed each other,

chunks.en: they may marry women fit for a Kohen.
chunks.st: they may marry women fit to marry into the priesthood, as a freed slave may marry such women. However, neither may marry a woman unfit for the priesthood, in case he is a priest.

chunks.en: They may not become tamei from the dead,
chunks.st: And they may not become ritually impure with impurity imparted by a corpse, since they are uncertain priests.

chunks.en: but if they did become tamei,
chunks.st: However, if they became impure,

chunks.en: they do not get the forty lashes.
chunks.st: they do not receive the forty lashes, as each of them might not be priest.

words.note: Forty lashes, a punishment of beis din.

chunks.en: They may not eat terumah,
chunks.st: And they may not partake of teruma, as one of them is not a priest.

chunks.en: but if they ate it,
chunks.st: However, if they ate teruma unwittingly

chunks.en: they do not pay back the amount plus a fifth.
chunks.st: they do not pay the principal and the additional fifth, as each of them might be a priest.

chunks.en: They do not get a share at the threshing floor.
chunks.st: And they do not receive a share of teruma in the granary, as neither can prove that he is a priest.

chunks.en: But they may sell their terumah,
chunks.st: However, they may sell the teruma that they remove from their own produce,

chunks.en: and the money is theirs.
chunks.st: and although they may not eat it, the money is theirs. Since it cannot be proven with regard to either of them that he is not a priest, teruma cannot be appropriated from them.

chunks.en: They do not get a share of the korbanos,
chunks.st: And they do not receive a share of the consecrated offerings of the Temple, as each of them might not be a priest.

chunks.en: and we do not give them korbanos to bring,
chunks.st: And one may not give them consecrated offerings to sacrifice for the same reason.

chunks.en: and we do not take their own away from them.
chunks.st: However, the hides of their own offerings may not be appropriated from their possession, as it cannot be proven with regard to either of them that he is not a priest.

chunks.en: They are free from giving the foreleg,
chunks.st: And they are exempt from giving a priest the foreleg, and from giving him

chunks.en: the jaw, and the stomach.
chunks.explain: Parts of an animal given to a Kohen.
chunks.st: the jaw, and from giving him the maw of their non-consecrated kosher animals.

chunks.en: And his bechor animal must graze until it gets a blemish,
chunks.st: And with regard to either of them, the firstling of his kosher animal should graze until it becomes unfit to be sacrificed, i.e., until it gets a blemish. It is against his interest to sacrifice the animal before it gets a blemish, thereby letting it be eaten by the priests. Once it gets a blemish, it cannot be appropriated from him. Since he is possibly a priest, he may claim that the animal is the property of a priest. The animal then becomes his private property, and he may eat it if he wishes. And in general,

words.note: A firstborn animal.

chunks.he: וְנוֹתְנִין עָלָיו חֻמְרֵי כֹהֲנִים וְחֻמְרֵי יִשְׂרְאֵלִים:
chunks.en: and we give him the strict rules of Kohanim and of Yisraelim.
chunks.st: we place upon him both the stringencies of priests and the stringencies of Israelites.

mishnayos.summary: A woman remarried too soon and had a baby, and no one knows which husband is the father. The mishnah teaches what this son and his half-brothers do about yibum.

chunks.en: A woman who did not wait after
chunks.st: With regard to a woman who did not wait

chunks.en: her husband three months, and remarried,
chunks.st: three months after separating from her husband, and remarried

chunks.he: וְיָלְדָה, וְאֵין יָדוּעַ אִם בֶּן תִּשְׁעָה
chunks.en: and gave birth, and we do not know if he is a nine-month baby
chunks.st: and gave birth to a son, and it is not known if he was born after nine months of pregnancy

chunks.en: from the first, or a seven-month baby from the second.
chunks.st: to the former husband or if he was born after seven months to the latter husband, if

chunks.en: If she had sons from
chunks.st: she had sons of certain patrilineage

chunks.en: the first and sons from the second,
chunks.st: from the first husband and sons of certain patrilineage from the second one, and the son of uncertain patrilineage married and died childless, then the brothers from both husbands

chunks.en: they do chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: must perform ḥalitza with his wife, as they might be his paternal brothers. But they may not perform levirate marriage with her, in case he is only their maternal half brother, and his wife is forbidden to them.

chunks.en: And so he, for them,
chunks.st: And similarly, with regard to him and their wives, if one of them dies childless,

chunks.en: does chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: he performs ḥalitza and not levirate marriage. If

chunks.he: הָיוּ לוֹ אַחִים מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן וְאַחִים
chunks.en: If he had brothers from the first and brothers
chunks.st: he had half brothers from the first husband and half brothers

chunks.en: from the second, not from the same mother,
chunks.st: from the second, not from the same mother but from the same father,

chunks.en: he may do chalitzah or yibum,
chunks.st: he performs ḥalitza or levirate marriage with their widows.
chunks.stMore: If he is indeed their paternal half brother, then the widows are his yevamot; if not, he may marry them like any other man.

chunks.en: and for them, one does chalitzah and one does yibum.
chunks.st: And similarly, with regard to them and his wife, one half brother from one father performs ḥalitza and one from the other father performs levirate marriage.

mishnayos.summary: If the son's possible fathers were a Kohen and a regular Jew, he gets the strict rules of both. If both were Kohanim, he mourns for both and they for him, with other special rules.

chunks.en: If one was a regular Jew and one a Kohen,
chunks.st: If one of his two uncertain fathers was an Israelite and one was a priest,

chunks.en: he marries a woman fit for a Kohen,
chunks.st: he may marry only a woman fit to marry a priest, due to the possibility that he is a priest.

chunks.en: and he may not become tamei from the dead,
chunks.st: And he may not become ritually impure with impurity imparted by a corpse because he might be a priest.

chunks.en: but if he became tamei,
chunks.st: But if he became impure,

chunks.en: he does not get the forty lashes.
chunks.st: he does not receive the forty lashes, as he might be a non-priest.

chunks.en: He may not eat terumah,
chunks.st: Likewise, he does not partake of teruma, in case he is a non-priest.

chunks.en: but if he ate it,
chunks.st: However, if he ate teruma

chunks.en: he does not pay back the amount plus a fifth.
chunks.st: he does not pay the principal and the additional fifth, as he might be a priest.

chunks.en: He does not get a share at the threshing floor.
chunks.st: And he does not receive teruma at the granary.

chunks.en: But he may sell the terumah,
chunks.st: However, he may sell the teruma of his own produce

chunks.en: and the money is his.
chunks.st: and the money is his. It cannot be taken away from him due to the uncertainty with regard to his status.

chunks.en: He does not get a share of the korbanos,
chunks.st: And he does not receive a share of the sacred of the consecrated offerings,

chunks.en: and we do not give him korbanos to bring,
chunks.st: and one may not give him the consecrated offerings to sacrifice.

mishnayos.stIntro: The Sages decreed that in the case of a minor girl whose father died, her mother or brothers may marry her off. However, such a marriage does not have the same legal status as the marriage of an adult. Therefore, if the minor regrets having married, she is allowed to make a declaration of refusal to her husband, thereby annulling the marital bond. The Sages disagreed with regard to the details of this halakha:

chunks.st: He marries his yevama and may never divorce her, as he does not have the legal capacity to end a valid marriage.

mishnayos.summary: A woman who traveled with her husband and came back saying he died is believed and may remarry, if there was peace at home and in the world. Rabbi Yehudah adds that she must come crying with torn clothes, but the Sages disagree.

chunks.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלְכָה הִיא וּבַעְלָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם,
chunks.en: A woman who went with her husband overseas,
chunks.st: With regard to a woman who went, she and her husband, overseas, if there was

chunks.en: when there was peace between them and peace in the world,
chunks.st: peace between him and her, i.e., the couple were not fighting at the time, and there was also peace in the world, i.e., there was no war at that time,

chunks.en: and she came back and said,
chunks.st: and the woman came back by herself and said:

chunks.en: "My husband died,"
chunks.st: My husband died,

chunks.en: she may marry. "My husband died,"
chunks.st: she may marry on the basis of her own testimony. Likewise, if she said: My husband died, and they did not have children, but her husband had a brother,

chunks.he: תִּתְיַבֵּם. שָׁלוֹם בֵּינוֹ לְבֵינָהּ וּמִלְחָמָה בָעוֹלָם,
chunks.en: she may do yibum. Peace between them but war in the world,

chunks.en: and she came back and said,
chunks.st: and she came and said:

chunks.en: "My husband died,"
chunks.st: My husband died,

chunks.en: she is not believed.
chunks.st: she is not deemed credible, as she may be mistaken or lying.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: she is never believed,
chunks.st: She is never deemed credible when she testifies that her husband died,

chunks.en: unless she came
chunks.st: unless she came

chunks.st: crying and her clothing was torn, in which case it is apparent that she is speaking the truth.

chunks.st: They said to him: This is an incorrect distinction. Rather,

chunks.st: both this woman who cries and this woman who does not cry may marry on the basis of their own testimony.

mishnayos.summary: Beis Hillel first said she is believed only if she came back from the grain harvest, like the story that happened. Beis Shammai said it is the same for any trip, and Beis Hillel agreed.

chunks.en: Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel say:

chunks.he: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ אֶלָּא בְּבָאָה מִן הַקָּצִיר,
chunks.en: "We only heard it about a woman coming from the harvest,
chunks.st: We heard that one may accept the testimony of a woman concerning the death of her husband only when she comes from the grain harvest,

chunks.en: and in that same country,
chunks.st: and when she testified in the same country where he died,

chunks.en: and like the story that happened."
chunks.st: and in circumstances similar to the incident that occurred, in which a lenient ruling was issued, as will be explained.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai said to them,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel: The same halakha applies to a wife

chunks.en: "Whether she comes from the grain harvest,
chunks.st: who comes from the grain harvest, and

chunks.en: or comes from the olives,
chunks.st: one who comes from the olive harvest,

chunks.en: or comes from the grape harvest,
chunks.st: and also one who comes from the grape harvest,

chunks.en: or comes from one country to another.
chunks.st: and even one who comes from one country to another country. Although the incident in question took place during the grain harvest,

chunks.he: לֹא דִבְּרוּ חֲכָמִים בַּקָּצִיר אֶלָּא בַהֹוֶה.
chunks.en: The Sages spoke of the harvest only because that is what happened."
chunks.st: the Sages spoke of the grain harvest only because it was the present occurrence, i.e., that is what happened in practice, but this is no proof that she is deemed credible only when she arrived specifically from the grain harvest. The mishna comments:

chunks.he: חָזְרוּ בֵית הִלֵּל לְהוֹרוֹת כְּבֵית שַׁמָּאי:
chunks.en: Beis Hillel changed their mind and taught like Beis Shammai.
chunks.st: Beit Hillel retracted their opinion, and decided to teach in accordance with the opinion of Beit Shammai on this issue.

mishnayos.summary: Beis Shammai say a woman who is believed that her husband died also gets her kesubah. Beis Hillel first argued, but they changed their mind and agreed.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
"She may marry and take her kesubah."
Beis Hillel say,
"She may marry, but not take her kesubah."
Beis Shammai said to them,
"You allowed a serious matter of a forbidden marriage;
will you not allow a light matter of money?"
Beis Hillel said to them,
"We see that the brothers do not take
the inheritance because of her word."
Beis Shammai said to them,
"We can learn from her kesubah document,
which he writes for her:
'If you marry another man,
take what is written for you.'"
And Beis Hillel changed their mind and taught
like Beis Shammai.

mishnayos.summary: Everyone is believed to say a woman's husband died, except some women who may dislike her. The mishnah also teaches what happens when witnesses disagree.

chunks.en: Everyone is believed to tell her,
chunks.st: All are deemed credible when they come to give testimony with regard to the death of a woman’s husband,

chunks.en: except her mother-in-law,
chunks.st: apart from her mother-in-law,

chunks.en: her mother-in-law's daughter,
chunks.st: the daughter of her mother-in-law,

chunks.en: her co-wife, her sister-in-law,
chunks.st: her rival wife, the wife of her yavam,

chunks.en: and her husband's daughter.
chunks.explain: These women may not like her, so they might lie.
chunks.st: and her husband’s daughter, her stepdaughter. The reason is that these women are likely to hate her and will lie to her detriment.

chunks.en: What is the difference between a get and a death?
chunks.st: The mishna explains: In the case of a divorce all people, including these women, may bring her bill of divorce and testify that it was written appropriately. What, then, is the difference between a bill of divorce and death? The mishna answers: The difference is that in the case of a bill of divorce

chunks.en: The writing proves it.
chunks.st: the writing proves the accuracy of the testimony, i.e., her testimony is supported by the text of the document itself, whereas with regard to the death of her husband there is no proof apart from the statement of the woman herself.

chunks.en: If one witness says he died,
chunks.st: If one witness says: The man died,

chunks.he: וְנִשֵּׂאת, וּבָא אַחֵר וְאָמַר לֹא מֵת,
chunks.en: and she married, and another came and said he did not die,
chunks.st: and the wife married based on this testimony, and one other witness came and said: He did not die,

chunks.en: she does not have to leave.
chunks.st: she need not leave her new husband due to this testimony.

chunks.en: If one witness says he died,
chunks.st: However, if one witness comes and says: The husband died,

chunks.en: and two say he did not die,
chunks.st: and two witnesses say: He did not die, then

chunks.en: even though she married,
chunks.st: even though she married based on the first witness

chunks.en: she must leave. If two say he died,
chunks.st: she must leave her new husband. If two witnesses say: He died,

chunks.en: and one witness says he did not die,
chunks.st: and one witness says: He did not die, the testimony of the two witnesses is accepted, and

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִשֵּׂאת, תִּנָּשֵׂא:
chunks.en: even though she has not married, she may marry.
chunks.st: even though she did not yet marry, she may marry.

mishnayos.summary: When two wives of the same man disagree about whether he died, each is treated by her own words. Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah argue when they disagree about how he died.

chunks.en: One wife says he died, and one
chunks.st: If two women who were married to the same man come forward, and one of them says that the husband died, and

chunks.en: says he did not die:
chunks.st: the other one says he did not die,

chunks.he: זוֹ שֶׁאוֹמֶרֶת מֵת תִּנָּשֵׂא וְתִטֹּל כְּתֻבָּתָהּ.
chunks.en: the one who says he died may marry and take her kesubah,
chunks.st: the one who says he died may marry on the basis of her own testimony, and she takes the money of her marriage contract.

chunks.en: and the one who says he did not die may not
chunks.st: And the one who said he did not die

chunks.en: marry, and does not take her kesubah.
chunks.st: may not marry, and does not take the money of her marriage contract. If

chunks.he: אַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת מֵת וְאַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת נֶהֱרָג,
chunks.en: If one says he died and one says he was killed,
chunks.st: one wife says: He died in a normal manner, and the other one says: He was killed,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: "Since they say different things,
chunks.st: Since they contradict one another,

chunks.en: they may not marry."
chunks.st: these women may not marry.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Shimon say,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon say:

chunks.he: הוֹאִיל וְזוֹ וָזוֹ מוֹדוֹת שֶׁאֵינוֹ קַיָּם,
chunks.en: "Since both agree he is not alive,
chunks.st: Since they both agree that he is not alive

chunks.en: they may marry." If one witness says he died and one witness
chunks.st: they may marry, despite the fact that they dispute the circumstances of his demise. If a witness says: He died, and a witness says:

chunks.en: says he did not die,
chunks.st: He did not die,

chunks.en: or one woman says he died and one woman
chunks.st: or one woman says: He died, and another

chunks.en: says he did not die,
chunks.st: woman says: He did not die,

chunks.en: she may not marry.
chunks.st: this woman may not marry.

mishnayos.summary: A woman who says her husband died may remarry, but her co-wife may not rely on her. Rabbi Tarfon lets the co-wife still eat terumah; Rabbi Akiva says she may neither remarry nor eat terumah.

chunks.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלְכָה הִיא וּבַעְלָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם,
chunks.en: A woman who went with her husband overseas,
chunks.st: In the case of a woman who went, she and her husband, overseas,

chunks.en: and came back and said, "My husband died,"
chunks.st: and she comes and says: My husband died,

chunks.en: may marry and take her kesubah,
chunks.st: she may marry, and she takes her marriage contract based on her own testimony.

chunks.en: but her co-wife is forbidden.
chunks.explain: A co-wife is not believed about the other wife.
chunks.st: And it remains prohibited for her rival wife to remarry, as a woman cannot testify on behalf of her rival wife.

chunks.en: If she was a Jewish woman married to a Kohen,
chunks.st: If the rival wife was an Israelite woman married to a priest,

chunks.en: she may eat terumah.
chunks.st: she may continue to partake of teruma, as she is not permitted to remarry, and therefore the presumption that the husband is still alive is maintained in relation to her. This is

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Tarfon says.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Tarfon.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.he: אֵין זוֹ דֶרֶךְ מוֹצִיאַתָּה מִידֵי עֲבֵרָה,
chunks.en: "This is not the way to keep her from sin,
chunks.st: This is not the way to spare someone from transgression.
chunks.stMore: According to the opinion of Rabbi Tarfon, there is a concern that she might be eating teruma unlawfully. There is no remedy for this situation

chunks.en: unless she is forbidden to marry
chunks.st: unless it is prohibited for the rival wife to marry, as she cannot rely on the testimony of her rival wife,

chunks.en: and forbidden to eat terumah."
chunks.st: and it is also prohibited for her to partake of teruma, lest the other woman was speaking the truth. In other words, the halakha is stringent on both counts.

mishnayos.summary: More arguments between Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva about avoiding sin: about a mother-in-law, about a man who married one of five women and does not know which, and about a man who stole from one of five people.

chunks.en: If she said, "My husband died, and after
chunks.st: The mishna discusses a similar case. If a woman said:

chunks.en: that my father-in-law died,"
chunks.st: My husband died and afterward my father-in-law died,

chunks.en: she may marry and take her kesubah,
chunks.st: she may marry and take her marriage contract,

chunks.en: but her mother-in-law is forbidden.
chunks.st: and it is prohibited for her mother-in-law to remarry, as a woman may not testify on behalf of her mother-in-law.

chunks.en: If she was a Jewish woman married to a Kohen,
chunks.st: If the mother-in-law was the daughter of an Israelite married to a priest,

chunks.en: she may eat terumah.
chunks.st: she may partake of teruma;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Tarfon says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Tarfon.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.he: אֵין זוֹ דֶרֶךְ מוֹצִיאַתָּה מִידֵי עֲבֵרָה,
chunks.en: "This is not the way to keep her from sin,
chunks.st: This is not the way to spare her from transgression; there is no remedy

chunks.en: unless she is forbidden to marry
chunks.st: unless it is prohibited for the mother-in-law to marry

chunks.en: and forbidden to eat terumah."
chunks.st: and also prohibited for her to partake of teruma.

chunks.en: If he made kiddushin with one of five women
chunks.st: In relation to the dispute between Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva in the previous mishna, in which Rabbi Akiva states that one must avoid a possible transgression, the mishna cites two similar cases involving other topics. With regard to one who betrothed one of five women,

chunks.en: and does not know which one,
chunks.st: and he does not know which of them he betrothed, and

chunks.en: and each one says, "He married me,"
chunks.st: each one of them says: He betrothed me, if he does not want to marry any of them

chunks.en: he gives a get to each one of them,
chunks.st: he gives a bill of divorce to each and every one of them so none will have the status of a woman with regard to whom there is uncertainty whether she is divorced.

chunks.en: and leaves one kesubah between them and goes away.
chunks.st: And he leaves the marriage contract among them and departs. The marriage contract remains in dispute between the women until they clarify which of them is entitled to the money. This is

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Tarfon says.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Tarfon.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.he: אֵין זוֹ דֶרֶךְ מוֹצִיאַתּוּ מִידֵי עֲבֵרָה,
chunks.en: "This is not the way to keep him from sin,
chunks.st: This is not the way to spare someone from transgression, as perhaps the woman he actually betrothed will not receive the money to which she is entitled. There is no remedy

chunks.en: unless he gives a get and a kesubah
chunks.st: unless he gives a bill of divorce and a marriage contract payment

chunks.en: to each one of them."
chunks.st: to each and every one.

chunks.en: If he stole from one of five people and does not
chunks.st: And likewise, in the case of one who stole money from one of five people

chunks.en: know from which one he stole,
chunks.st: and does not know from which of them he stole, and

chunks.en: and each one says, "He stole from me,"
chunks.st: each one says: He stole from me,

chunks.en: he leaves the stolen money between them and goes away.
chunks.st: he leaves the stolen money among them and departs, and they will decide among themselves how to distribute the money; this is

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Tarfon says.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Tarfon.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.he: אֵין זוֹ דֶרֶךְ מוֹצִיאַתּוּ מִידֵי עֲבֵרָה,
chunks.en: "This is not the way to keep him from sin,
chunks.st: This is not the way to spare him from transgression; there is no remedy

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁיְּשַׁלֵּם גְּזֵלָה לְכָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד:
chunks.en: unless he pays back each one of them."
chunks.st: unless he pays each and every one of them.

mishnayos.summary: A woman traveled with her husband and son and came back alone. If she says her husband died first, she is believed and is free. If she says her son died first, she is not believed for yibum, so she does chalitzah.

chunks.en: A woman who went with her husband
chunks.st: In the case of a woman who went, she and her husband,

chunks.en: overseas, and her son was with them,
chunks.st: overseas, and her son was with them, and later

chunks.en: and she came back and said, "My husband died,
chunks.st: she came back and said: My husband died

chunks.en: and after that my son died,"
chunks.st: and afterward my son died,

chunks.he: נֶאֱמֶנֶת. מֵת בְּנִי וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת בַּעְלִי,
chunks.en: she is believed. "My son died, and after that my husband died,"
chunks.st: she is deemed credible. It is permitted for her to remarry, and she is exempt from levirate marriage. The reason is that she had children when she left, and therefore she retains her presumptive status of one who is exempt from levirate marriage. However, if she said: My son died and afterward my husband died,

chunks.en: she is not believed.
chunks.st: she is not deemed credible, i.e., she may not enter into levirate marriage.

chunks.en: But we worry about her words,
chunks.st: And yet we are concerned and give some credence to her statement, in case she was actually widowed by a childless husband, and therefore

chunks.en: so she does chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: she performs ḥalitza to exempt her from the levirate bond with her yavam, and she does not enter into levirate marriage.

mishnayos.summary: A woman says she had a son overseas. If she says the son died before her husband, she is believed. If she says her husband died first, she is not believed, but she still needs chalitzah.

chunks.en: "A son was born to me overseas,"
chunks.st: If she went with her childless husband and returned alone and testified: A son was born to me overseas,

chunks.en: and she said, "My son died, and after
chunks.st: and she further said: My son died

chunks.en: that my husband died,"
chunks.st: and afterward my husband died,

chunks.he: נֶאֱמֶנֶת. מֵת בַּעְלִי וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת בְּנִי,
chunks.en: she is believed. "My husband died, and after that my son died,"
chunks.st: she is deemed credible and may even enter into levirate marriage, as she was presumed to be childless when she left and consequently she retains that presumptive status. However, if she said: My husband died and afterward my son died,

chunks.en: she is not believed.
chunks.st: she is not deemed credible for the purpose of exempting her from levirate marriage,

chunks.en: But we worry about her words,
chunks.st: but the court is concerned about her statement.

chunks.en: so she does chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: And therefore she must perform ḥalitza and she does not enter into levirate marriage.

mishnayos.summary: A woman is believed about a brother-in-law born overseas. But if they all left together, she is not believed that the yavam died, and a person is not believed when his words would let him marry someone.

chunks.en: "A yavam was born to me overseas,"
chunks.st: If she said: A yavam was born for me overseas, i.e., when the family left the country her husband did not have a brother, and she claims that in the meantime a brother was born to her husband,

chunks.en: and she said, "My husband died, and after
chunks.st: and she also said: My husband died

chunks.en: that my yavam died,"
chunks.st: and afterward my yavam died, or:

chunks.en: or "my yavam, and after that my husband,"
chunks.st: My yavam died and afterward my husband died, in either case

chunks.he: נֶאֱמֶנֶת. הָלְכָה הִיא וּבַעְלָהּ וִיבָמָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם,
chunks.en: she is believed. If she, her husband, and her yavam went overseas,
chunks.st: she is deemed credible. This is because when she left she was not presumed to require levirate marriage, and the suggestion that her husband now has a brother is based solely on her testimony. However, if she went, she and her husband and her yavam, overseas, and upon her return she

chunks.en: and she said, "My husband died, and after
chunks.st: said: My husband died and afterward

chunks.en: that my yavam died,"
chunks.st: my yavam died, or:

chunks.en: or "my yavam, and after that my husband,"
chunks.st: My yavam died and afterward my husband died,

chunks.en: she is not believed.
chunks.st: she is not deemed credible, as

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין הָאִשָּׁה נֶאֱמֶנֶת לוֹמַר מֵת יְבָמִי,
chunks.en: A woman is not believed to say, "My yavam died,"
chunks.st: a woman is not deemed credible if she says: My yavam died, in order

chunks.en: so that she can marry. Nor,
chunks.st: that she may marry another man. And she is not deemed credible if she says that

chunks.en: "My sister died,"
chunks.st: her sister died, in order

chunks.en: so that she can marry her husband.
chunks.st: that she may enter the house of her sister’s husband.

chunks.he: וְאֵין הָאִישׁ נֶאֱמָן לוֹמַר מֵת אָחִי,
chunks.en: And a man is not believed to say, "My brother died,"
chunks.st: And a man is not deemed credible if he says: My brother died,

chunks.en: so that he can do yibum with his wife.
chunks.st: so that he may enter into levirate marriage with his brother’s wife,

chunks.en: Nor, "My wife died,"
chunks.st: and he is not deemed credible when he says that his wife died,

chunks.en: so that he can marry her sister.
chunks.st: in order that he may marry his wife’s sister. The Sages accepted impaired testimony of this kind only when there was a concern about creating a situation of a deserted wife.

mishnayos.summary: A woman hears that her husband died overseas, where he was with her co-wife. She must wait to see if the co-wife is expecting a baby, because then she would be free of yibum. The mishnah also asks about a mother-in-law who left while expecting.

chunks.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלַךְ בַּעְלָהּ וְצָרָתָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם,
chunks.en: A woman whose husband and co-wife went overseas,
chunks.st: In the case of a woman whose husband and rival wife traveled to a country overseas, and witnesses

chunks.en: and people came and told her, "Your husband died":
chunks.st: came and told her: Your husband died,

chunks.en: she may not marry and may not do yibum
chunks.st: she shall not marry any other man, in case she requires levirate marriage with her brother-in-law, i.e., yavam, in which case she is prohibited from marrying anyone else.

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁתֵּדַע שֶׁמָּא מְעֻבֶּרֶת הִיא צָרָתָהּ.
